statement.name: Parallelization of well-foundedness / hyperjump
statement.definition: WF(T)=1 iff the tree T is well-founded; WF-hat is its parallelization, strongly Weihrauch equivalent to the hyperjump HJ, the analogue of Π11-CA0 (the catalogue only has chipi11, the single WF).
statement.facts: WF-hat ≡sW HJ (Lemma 3.6), ≡sW β-mod (Prop 3.12); HJ^n ≡sW HJ^[n] (Lemma 5.1); WF-hat is not Weihrauch reducible to Σ0α-RT for any α<ω1 (Cor 5.23).

statement.name: β-model function
statement.definition: Maps X to a pair (W,h) where W codes a countable β-model containing X and h is a Skolem function for Π01 predicates with parameters in W.
statement.facts: β-mod ≡sW WF-hat (Prop 3.12); it is a cylinder.

statement.notation: Γ-RT (Galvin–Prikry), Γ in {Σ0n, Π0n, Δ0n, Σ0α}
statement.name: Galvin-Prikry Ramsey property for Borel classes (problem and schema)
statement.definition: Γ-RT: given A in Γ([ω]^ω), find an infinite homogeneous set for A. The schema versions express that all Γ-definable sets of the Ramsey space are Ramsey.
statement.facts: Σ0k-RT ≤sW WF-hat^[k] (Lemma 5.4); Σ0_{k+1}-RT ≤W Σ0_k-RT ⋆ WF-hat (Lemma 5.5); Σ0_{k+1}-RT <W Σ01-RT ⋆ WF-hat^[k] (Cor 5.24); Σ01-RT ≤sW WF-hat (Cor 5.3); Π11-CA0 proves Σ0k-RT (Cor 2.11); RCA0+Δ02-RT proves Π11-CA0; Σ0_{ω+α}-RT ≤W Σ01-RT ⋆ HJ^{ω^{1+α}} (Prop 5.30); Σ0n-RT is a strictly increasing chain in arithmetical Weihrauch degrees; lightface Σ0_{k+1}/Δ0_{k+1} Galvin-Prikry equivalent over β-models to existence of HJ^k(∅) (Thm 6.1).

statement.name: One-sided and weak one-sided homogeneous set functions
statement.definition: FindHS_Γ(A)=HS(A)∩A on sets having a homogeneous set landing in A; wFindHS_Γ is its restriction to sets all of whose homogeneous sets land in A (catalogue has these only for Γ=Σ01, Π01, Δ01).
statement.facts: wFindHSΣ0_{k+1} ≡aW UC ⋆ WF-hat^[k]; wFindHSΠ0_{k+1} ≡aW C_{ω^ω} ⋆ WF-hat^[k] (Prop 5.13); wFindHSΣ0_{k+1} <aW wFindHSΠ0_{k+1}; WF-hat^[k] <aW wFindHSΔ0_{k+1} (Prop 5.10); wFindHSΠ0_{k+1} <W FindHSΠ0_{k+1} (Cor 5.28); Σ0_{k+1}-RT ≤aW FindHSΣ0_{k+1}; FindHSΣ0_{k+1} is not aW-below Σ01-RT ⋆ WF-hat^[k].

statement.name: Weak König's lemma for Δ^0_n-definable trees
statement.definition: For every Δ^0_n-set that is an infinite 0–1 tree there is a Δ^0_n-set that is an infinite path in it.
statement.facts: Δ^0_1-WKL is equivalent to WKL over RCA*_0. Belanger showed Δ^0_2-WKL is equivalent to COH over RCA_0 + BΣ^0_2. Δ^0_n-WKL implies BΣ^0_n over RCA*_0 (Proposition 4.4). Δ^0_n-WKL is Π^1_1-conservative over RCA*_0 + BΣ^0_n, and countable topped models of RCA*_0 + BΣ^0_n ω-extend to models of it (Lemma 4.5).

statement.name: ≪^n_A-basis theorem and the sentence γ_ψ
statement.definition: X ≪^n_A Y says every Δ_n(X⊕A) infinite 0–1 tree has a Δ_n(Y⊕A) path. The ≪^n_A-basis theorem for ψ = ∀X∃Yα says that if X ≪^n_A Z there is a Δ_n(Z⊕A) set Y with α(X,Y) and X⊕Y ≪^n_A Z.
statement.facts: A Π^1_2 sentence ψ is Π^1_1-conservative over RCA*_0 + BΣ^0_n + ¬IΣ^0_n iff RCA*_0 + BΣ^0_n proves γ_ψ. The paper also shows RCA_0 + RT^2_2 proves the ≪^2_∅-basis theorem for RT^2_2.

statement.name: Comparability of well-orderings (problems) and weak comparability
statement.definition: Given two well-orderings, produce an embedding of one onto an initial segment of the other (CWO), or an embedding of one into the other (WCWO).
statement.facts: WCWO ≤W CWO. CWO ≤W ATR (Prop. 4.5). ATR ≤W WCWO (Thm 6.3), so WCWO ≡W CWO ≡W ATR ≡W UCNN (Cor. 6.4), answering Marcone's question.

statement.name: Fraïssé's conjecture problems for linear orders and well-orderings, no infinite descending sequence, no infinite antichain
statement.definition: WQOLO and WQOWO: given a sequence of linear orders (well-orders), produce i<j and an embedding from Li into Lj. NDSWO: given well-orders and embeddings from Li+1 into Li, produce i<j and an embedding from Li into Lj. NIACWO: given well-orders, produce i, j (possibly i>j) and an embedding from Li into Lj.
statement.facts: NDSWO ≤W WQOWO ≤W WQOLO, and NIACWO ≤W WCWO ≤W CWO and NIACWO ≤W WQOWO. WQOWO ≤W ATR. ATR ≤W CN ∗ NDSWO and ATR ≤W CN ∗ NIACWO, hence ATR ≤c and ≤arith_W for each. ATR ≤c WQOLO. WQOLO ≤W CNN but CNN is not arithmetically W-reducible to WQOLO, and WQOLO is not computably or arithmetically W-reducible to UCNN. Open whether ATR ≤W NDSWO, NIACWO or WQOWO.

statement.name: Two-sided König duality theorem problem
statement.definition: Given a graph, produce an odd cycle or a König cover.
statement.facts: KDT2 ≤W LPO × KDT, hence KDT ≡W KDT2 (Prop. 9.5).

statement.name: Perfect set theorem problem on a computable Polish space X
statement.definition: Given an uncountable closed set A ⊆ X, find a perfect closed subset P ⊆ A.
statement.facts: PST_{2^N} ≡sW PST_{N^N} (Thm 3.3). UC_{N^N} <sW PST_{N^N} <sW C_{N^N} (Thm 3.6). PST_{N^N} ≰W UC_{N^N}. The first-order part of PST_{N^N} is Π11-C_N (Lemma 3.5). PST_{[0,1]} ≡W PST_{N^N} (Thm 5.6), and PST_R ≡W PST_{N^N} (Remark 5.7). PST_{N^N} ≤W PST_X for any rich X (Lemma 5.5).

statement.name: One-sided perfect tree theorem restricted to binary trees
statement.definition: PTT_1 restricted to binary trees.
statement.facts: PTT_1↾Tr_2 ≡sW PTT_1 (Thm 3.3). It is Weihrauch equivalent to C_{N^N} (via [18, Prop. 6.3]) and ≤W lim ∗ PST_{2^N}.

statement.name: Perfect kernel function
statement.definition: The total single-valued function sending a tree (or closed set) to its perfect kernel.
statement.facts: WF-hat ≡sW PK (Hirst, Thm 4.2). PK_{N^N} ≡W WF-hat_S, where WF_S is the Sierpiński-space version of WF (Thm 4.9). PK_{2^N} ≡sW PK_{N^N}, and both are strongly parallelizable and cylinders. PK_{N^N} <W PK ≤W lim ∗ PK_{N^N}; whether PK ≡W lim ∗ PK_{N^N} is open. PK_{N^N} is incomparable with C_{N^N}, and PK_{N^N} <W TC-bar_{N^N}. Det(PK_{N^N}) ≡W UC_{N^N}. The first-order part of PK_{N^N} is Π11-C_N. PK_X ≡W PK_{N^N} for every rich computable Polish space X (Thm 5.18).

statement.name: Listing problems for countable closed sets
statement.definition: Given a countable closed set A, list its elements. The weak versions omit the cardinality; the others also output |A|.
statement.facts: Theorem 3.10 and Figure 2. wList_{2^N} is parallelizable, and its first-order part is C_N (Lemmas 3.11, 3.12). wList_R ≡W wList_{[0,1]} ≡W wList_{2^N}. wList_N ≡W lim and wList_N <W List_N. List_n ≡W wList_n ≡W LPO^n.

statement.name: Scattered-part listing and counting problems
statement.definition: Given a closed set A, list the elements of its scattered part (the weak versions give no cardinality), or output the code of its cardinality (ScCount).
statement.facts: wScList_{N^N} ≡W PK_{N^N} (Thm 4.25). PK_{N^N} <W ScList_{N^N} <W WF-hat (Thms 4.27, 4.29). The first-order part of wScList_{2^N} is Π02-C_N (Lemma 4.31). Theorem 4.32 gives the relations for the Cantor-space versions. ScCount_X ≤W Π04-C_N for computably Kσ spaces. Problems 6.2–6.4 are open.

statement.name: Cantor–Bendixson problems
statement.definition: Output the perfect kernel together with the list (and cardinality, for CB) of the scattered part of a closed set or tree.
statement.facts: wCB ≡W CB ≡W WF-hat (Prop 4.34). wCB_{2^N} ≡W CB_{2^N} ≡W PK_{N^N} <W ScList_{N^N} ≤W CB_{N^N} <W CB (Thm 4.35). CB_{N^N} ≤W WF^{u*} × PK_{N^N} ≤W C_N ∗ PK_{N^N} (Thm 4.36). wCB_X ≡W PK_{N^N} for rich X, and CB_X ≡W PK_{N^N} for rich computably Kσ X. CB_{N^N} ≤W CB_X when X is computably non-Kσ.

items.quote: Conidis [4, Theorem 3.1] constructed a standard model which satisfies ∆11 -CA0 but not ABW0.
reasons: attributed by the paper to Conidis [4, Theorem 3.1]: cite the original

statement.notation: IRT_XYZ (X in U/D, Y in V/E, Z in S/D)
statement.name: Variants of the infinite ray theorem (undirected/directed, vertex/edge-disjoint, single/double rays)
statement.definition: Every X-graph with arbitrarily many Y-disjoint Z-rays has infinitely many Y-disjoint Z-rays. Catalogue irt presumably corresponds to IRT_UVS.
statement.facts: IRT_XYS and IRT_UVD are theorems of hyperarithmetic analysis and provable in Σ11-AC0 (Theorem 5.1). Every variant implies ACA0 (Theorem 5.9). IRT_DYZ implies IRT_UYZ, IRT_DEZ implies IRT_DVZ, and IRT_DYD implies IRT_DYS over RCA0. IRT_UVD implies IRT_UVS over RCA0 + IΣ11 (Theorem 6.15). IRT_DED and IRT_DVD are open, and IRT_UED is due to Bowler–Carmesin–Pott. On directed forests IRT_DED + IΣ11 is equivalent to Σ11-AC0 + IΣ11 (Theorem 6.13).

statement.name: Maximum cardinality infinite ray theorem
statement.definition: Every X-graph has a set of Y-disjoint Z-rays of maximum cardinality.
statement.facts: Equivalent to IRT_XYZ over RCA0 + IΣ11 (Proposition 6.3). It proves ACA*0 (Theorem 6.8), hence the consistency of Σ11-AC0, so it is not provable in Σ11-AC0 (Corollary 9.? is Corollary 6.9), and it is strictly stronger than IRT for XYS and UVD (Corollary 6.10). It implies finite-Σ11-AC0 and ABW0 (Theorems 7.3, 7.7). IRT*_DVD and IRT*_DED on directed forests are equivalent to Σ11-AC0 + IΣ11 (Theorem 6.13), and IRT*_UVD implies IRT_UVS over RCA0 (Theorem 6.15).

statement.name: Maximal infinite ray theorem
statement.definition: Every X-graph has a possibly finite sequence of Y-disjoint Z-rays that is maximal under inclusion.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Π11-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.18).

statement.name: Strongly collecting rays; nonuniform weak infinite ray theorem
statement.definition: SCR: from arbitrarily many Y-disjoint Z-rays one obtains a sequence whose k-th entry is a set of k disjoint rays. Nonuniform-WIRT: WIRT with a sequence of rays such that for each k some k+1 of them are disjoint.
statement.facts: SCR_XYZ implies ACA0. SCR_XYZ is equivalent to IRT_XYZ over RCA0 for XYS and UVD (Corollary 8.5). Nonuniform-WIRT_XYS and nonuniform-WIRT_UVD are equivalent to ACA0 (Theorem 8.9).

statement.name: Σ11 choice with unique solutions
statement.definition: (∀n)(∃!X)A(n,X) → (∃Y)(∀n)A(n,Y^[n]) for arithmetic A.
statement.facts: Implied by finite-Σ11-AC0 and a theorem of hyperarithmetic analysis. Strictly weaker than finite-Σ11-AC0 (Goh).

statement.name: Σ11 induction
statement.definition: The induction scheme for Σ11 formulas.
statement.facts: IRT_XYZ + IΣ11 is equivalent to IRT*_XYZ. Σ11-AC0 and ATR0 do not prove IΣ11.

statement.name: Hindman's theorem for 2 colors
statement.definition: Hindman's theorem restricted to colorings of N with 2 colors.
statement.facts: Proposition III.43: HT2 implies HT over RCA0, by induction on the number of colors.

statement.name: Existence of right-matches, left-matches and full-matches
statement.definition: For every k-coloring c of N and infinite S there is a right-match (resp. left-match, full-match) (F,T) with F ∪ T ⊆ S, in the sense of Towsner's matches. RM_k, LM_k, FM_k are the versions with fixed k.
statement.facts: Theorem III.30 / Corollary III.30.2: right-matches exist computably in (c,S), uniformly in (c,S)'' (RCA0 proves Theorem III.11). Theorem III.40: no continuous functional maps a coloring to a right-match. Theorem III.41: every 2-coloring has a left-match computable uniformly in (c,S)''. Proposition III.44: RM_2 implies RM and FM_2 implies FM over RCA0. Corollary III.31.2: full-matches exist in ACA0. Whether every computable coloring has a computable full-match is open (Question III.54), as is whether LM_2 implies LM_k (Question III.45).

statement.name: Transfinite induction schemes for Π¹ₙ formulas
statement.definition: RCA0 plus transfinite induction along well-orders for formulas in Γ.
statement.facts: Σ⁰₁-TI0 is equivalent to ACA0 and contained in ATR0. Π¹₁-TI0 is not contained in ATR0, which is strictly contained in Σ¹₁-TI0. Π¹₁-TI0 is equivalent to Σ¹₁-DC0. ACA0 + ωX-RFN for Σ¹₁₊ₙ is equivalent to Π¹ₙ-TI0 (Theorem 3 and Theorem 7).

statement.notation: CSC space statements (T3 CSC metrizable, orderable, etc.)
statement.name: Topological characterization theorems for countable second countable spaces
statement.definition: Statements about countable second countable (CSC) topological spaces in Dorais's formalization: every regular eT2 CSC space is uniformly regular, T3 CSC space is metrizable or orderable, compact T2 CSC space is well-orderable, locally compact T2 CSC space has a choice of compact neighborhoods, T3 scattered CSC space has a Cantor-Bendixson rank, is completely metrizable, embeds into a well order, and so on.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, arithmetic comprehension is equivalent to many statements: every T3 eT2 CSC space is metrizable or has an algebra of clopen sets, every T3 CSC space is homeomorphic to a linear order, every compact CSC space is effectively compact. ACA0 proves every T3 CSC space is homeomorphic to a linear order and every compact T2 CSC space is homeomorphic to a well-order. Arithmetic transfinite recursion is equivalent over RCA0 to: every locally compact T2 CSC space has a choice of compact neighborhoods or is well-orderable, every T3 scattered CSC space embeds into a well order, has a Cantor-Bendixson rank, or is completely metrizable (Bel'nov-Knaster-Urbanik, Katetov), and to topological comparability of locally compact T2 CSC spaces. Π11 comprehension is equivalent over RCA0 to: the set of indices of compact, connected, scattered, or complete spaces exists; every T3 CSC space is ranked; every T3 CSC space splits into a scattered and a dense-in-itself subspace. The statements TAM and 1TAM about eventually well-founded tree arrays: TAM is equivalent to a statement about eventually well-ordered sequences of linear orders and is provable in ATR0, and 1TAM implies ATR0 over RCA0.

statement.notation: Σ¹₁-C_X, Σ¹₁-tree-C_X, Π⁰ₙ-C_{2^ω}, C_{2^ω}, C_{ω^ω} (Σ¹₁-presentation choice problems)
statement.name: Choice on analytic and arithmetical sets in Cantor/Baire space
statement.loc: Definition IV.11, Example IV.12, Theorems IV.13–IV.15
statement.definition: Given a presentation of a nonempty closed, Σ¹₁ or Π⁰ₙ set (or a Σ¹₁ tree), find an element or a path.
statement.facts: Σ¹₁-C_{ω^ω} ≡ Σ¹₁-tree-C_{ω^ω} ≡ C_{ω^ω} ≡ Σ¹₁-C_{2^ω} (IV.13). For n ≥ 2, C_{2^ω} ≡ Π⁰₁-C_{2^ω} <W Π⁰ₙ-C_{2^ω} ≡ Σ¹₁-C_{2^ω} (IV.14). C_{2^ω} <W Σ¹₁-WKL <W Σ¹₁-C_{2^ω} (IV.15).

statement.notation: Σ¹₁-UC_X, Σ¹₁-KC_X, Σ¹₁-C^fin, Σ¹₁-C^cof, Σ¹₁-C^foc, Σ¹₁-C^aof, Σ¹₁-C^aou, Σ¹₁-UC^tot
statement.name: Restricted Σ¹₁ single choice principles
statement.definition: Σ¹₁ choice restricted to singletons, compact, finite, cofinite, finite-or-cofinite, all-or-finite or all-or-unique sets. UC^tot is the totalization of unique choice.
statement.facts: Σ¹₁-UC_{ω^ω} <W Σ¹₁-KC_{ω^ω} ≡W Σ¹₁-WKL (IV.17). Parallelized Σ¹₁-C_2 ≡W Π¹₁-Tot2 ≡W Π¹₁-DNC2 (IV.18). Parallelized Σ¹₁-C^aou_N ≡W Π¹₁-Tot_N (IV.19). UC^tot_X ≡W C^aou_X for Δ¹₁ X (IV.27); parallelized Σ¹₁-UC^tot_2 ≡W Σ¹₁-WKL (IV.27.1).

statement.name: Π¹₁ totalization and diagonalization problems
statement.definition: Totalize a partial Π¹₁ function (2-valued or N-valued), or find a function diagonalizing a sequence of partial Π¹₁ functions.
statement.facts: Π¹₁-DNC_N ≤W Π¹₁-DNC2 ≡W Π¹₁-Tot2 ≤W Π¹₁-Tot_N, and the equivalences in IV.18 and IV.19.

statement.notation: Σ¹₁-AC_X, Σ¹₁-DC_X and restrictions Σ¹₁-AC^?_N, Σ¹₁-DC^?_N (? ∈ {fin, cof, foc, aof, aou})
statement.name: Σ¹₁ axioms of choice and dependent choice (Weihrauch problems)
statement.definition: AC is the parallelization of Σ¹₁ choice, giving an element of the product of nonempty Σ¹₁ sets. DC is the dependent version, giving a path through a Σ¹₁ tree of choices. The superscript restricts the type of sets.
statement.facts: Σ¹₁-DC_X ≡W Σ¹₁-tree-C_X (IV.22). Σ¹₁-AC_2 ≡W Σ¹₁-DC2 ≡W Σ¹₁-WKL <W Σ¹₁-C_{2^ω}, and Σ¹₁-AC_ω ≤W Σ¹₁-DC_ω ≡W Σ¹₁-C_{ω^ω} (IV.24). AC^fin ≡W DC^fin (IV.30). AC^aou ≡W AC^aof ≡W AC^fosc (IV.35.1). AC^aof ≡W DC^aof (IV.36.1). AC^fin <W AC^aof (IV.38.1). AC^cof is Weihrauch incomparable with AC^fin and AC^aof (IV.41.1). There are upward density and maximum Medvedev degree results (IV.31, IV.37, IV.42, IV.45.1) and downward density of Σ¹₁-DC_N (IV.46). Σ¹₁-ATR2 ≰W Σ¹₁-AC_ω (IV.100), hence Σ¹₁-AC_ω ≰W Σ¹₁-DC_ω (IV.100.1), answering Question IV.25.

statement.name: Weihrauch versions of ATR
statement.definition: ATR: given a well-order E and an arithmetical Φ, output a hierarchy for Φ on E. ATR2': like ATR2, but a jump hierarchy may be on an initial segment containing the well-founded part. ATR2^po: ATR2 for partial orders.
statement.facts: ATR ≡W Σ¹₁-UC_{ω^ω} (IV.76). ATR <W ATR2' ≤W ATR2 ≤W ATR2^po (IV.72). ATR2^po <W C_{ω^ω} (IV.77). Parallelized ATR2' ≡aW Σ¹₁-KC_{N^N} ≡aW parallelized Σ¹₁-C^aou_N (IV.65). Σ¹₁-C^aou_N ≤W ATR2^po (IV.69). Robustness results (IV.61, IV.63) are cited from Goh.

statement.name: Unbounded ATR and method of pseudo-hierarchies
statement.definition: Given an arithmetical Φ and a halting condition Ψ, find an ordinal and a hierarchy satisfying Ψ. For MPH, the alternative is an ill-founded order with a pseudo-hierarchy that never satisfies Ψ.
statement.facts: MPH is equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (IV.58, IV.59). ATR2 <W ATRunb and ATR2^po <W ATRunb (IV.73). C_{ω^ω} ≤W MPH and C_{ω^ω} ≤W ATRunb (IV.78). PTT_det ≤W ATRunb (IV.83). It is open whether ATRunb ≡W MPH (Question IV.75).

statement.name: Weihrauch-problem versions of ATR0-level theorems
statement.definition: PTT_list: enumerate a superset of [T]. PTT_det: a perfect subtree or an enumeration covering [T]. CWO: compare two well-orders by an embedding onto an initial segment. WCWO: embedding not necessarily onto an initial segment. Σ¹₁-Sep: separate two disjoint Σ¹₁-described sets of N.
statement.facts: ATR ≡W Σ¹₁-Sep <W Π¹₁-Sep ≡W Σ¹₁-WKL (IV.80, cited). ATR ≡W PTT_list <W PTT_1 <W PTT_det (IV.82, cited). CWO ≡W ATR ≡W WCWO (IV.85, cited).

items.quote: (2) the functions C2ω , lim, Cωω and UCωω are all cylinders,
items.concerns: The paper calls these 'well-known facts' and gives no explicit citation.
reasons: attributed by the paper to well-known facts (cf. [BGP21]): cite the original

statement.name: Laver Partition Theorem for open (resp. clopen) sets
statement.definition: For every open (resp. clopen) set A ⊆ ω^ω there is a Laver tree T' with empty stem such that [T'] ⊆ A or [T'] ∩ A = ∅. Also considered as problems whose solutions are codes of Laver trees.
statement.facts: Σ01-RT implies LLΣ01 and Δ01-RT implies LLΔ01 over RCA0 (Lemma 1.1). Σ01-DET implies LLΣ01 over RCA0 (Lemma 1.2). LLΔ01 implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Lemma 4.1). RCA0 + finitary Σ11-AC0 + LLΔ01 proves Δ11-CA0 (Prop. 4.5). RCA0 + finitary Σ11-AC0 + LLΣ01 proves Σ11-AC0 (Prop. 4.6). Over RCA0 + Σ11-IND, LLΔ01 implies Δ11-CA0 and LLΣ01 implies Σ11-AC0 (Thm 1.7). LLΔ01 ≡sW UC_{ω^ω} (Thm 5.3). TC_{ω^ω} ≤W C_{2^ω} ⋆ LLΣ01 (Lemma 5.12). TC_{ω^ω} <aW LLΣ01 (Prop. 5.15). LLΣ01 ≰W C_{ω^ω} (Cor. 5.13). Computability bounds: Thm 1.9, Thm 1.10, Cor. 3.4, Cor. 3.5.

statement.name: Hechler–Laver principles
statement.definition: For every open set A there is either a Hechler tree T with [T] ⊆ A or a Laver tree S with [S] ∩ A = ∅ (HLΣ01). The dual version for Π01 is HLΠ01, and HLΔ01 is the analogous clopen version.
statement.facts: ATR0 proves HLΣ01 and HLΠ01 (Thm 1.5, Thm 3.2). Over RCA0, ATR0 is equivalent to HLΔ01 (and HLΣ01, HLΠ01) (Thm 1.8, Lemma 4.4). HLΣ01 or HLΠ01 implies LLΣ01, and HLΔ01 implies LLΔ01.

statement.name: Find-Laver-tree problems
statement.definition: Given A ∈ Γ(ω^ω), find a code of a Laver tree T with [T] ⊆ A. The domain of FindL is the A for which such a tree exists; the domain of wFindL is the A meeting every Laver tree.
statement.facts: wFindLΔ01, wFindLΣ01, LLΔ01, FindLΔ01 and FindLΣ01 are all ≡sW UC_{ω^ω} (Thm 5.3). FindLΠ01 ≡sW C_{ω^ω} (Prop. 5.4). C_{2^ω} ⋆ wFindLΠ01 ≡W C_{ω^ω} (Prop. 5.5). wFindLΠ01 is not a cylinder, hence wFindLΠ01 ≢sW FindLΠ01 (Thm 5.10). wFindLΠ01 is parallelizable (Prop. 5.11).

statement.name: Finitary Σ11 choice
statement.definition: The schema ∀i ∃f φ(i,f) → ∀n ∃g ∀i ≤ n φ(i, g_i) for Σ11 formulas φ.
statement.facts: Implied over RCA0 by both Σ11-AC0 and Σ11-IND (Lemma 2.7). Used as a base theory for partial reversals.

statement.name: Closed choice on a represented space X
statement.definition: Given a nonempty closed subset of X by negative information (an enumeration of its complement), find a point of it.
statement.facts: Characterizes the classes of computable functions (X={0}), finitely many mind changes (X=N), weakly computable functions (X Cantor space), and effectively Borel measurable functions (X Baire space). C_{N×{0,1}^N} ≡W C_R. Proves C_Q ≡W C_N, C_{R\Q} ≡W C_{N^N}. Choice on Polish spaces falls into the dichotomy C_R-below or C_{N^N}-equivalent. Also: C_{{0,1}}×C_{{0,1}} <W C_{{0,1}×{0,1}}.

statement.name: Low representation / low computability operator
statement.definition: Single-valued map on Baire space whose computable inputs yield exactly the low points.
statement.facts: f is low computable iff f ≤sW L (Theorem 8.10). C_{{0,1}^N} ≤sW L; C_{N×{0,1}^N} ≤sW L and L ≰W C_{N×{0,1}^N}. L <W lim. L <W L×L, so L is not idempotent. Composition of a low computable map with a limit computable map is limit computable.

statement.name: Limit with respect to the initial topology of the jump (Π-topology)
statement.definition: lim_J = J^{-1}∘lim∘J^N, the limit operator on Baire space with respect to the initial topology of the Turing jump J.
statement.facts: lim_J <sW L, and lim_J ≡sW L relative to some oracle. C_{{0,1}^N} ≰W lim_J. lim_∆ <W lim_J <W lim. Points limit computable in the jump are low and do not bound DNC functions.

statement.name: Discrete limit
statement.definition: Limit of eventually constant sequences in Baire space.
statement.facts: lim_∆ ≡W C_N (Corollary 7.12); f ≤W lim_∆ iff f is computable with finitely many mind changes.

statement.notation: mPH^n_k, ItPH^n_k, PH^n_k, PH^n, PH (second-order and first-order variants)
statement.name: Paris–Harrington principle variants (m-density, iterated)
statement.definition: For any infinite set X0 (first-order version: for any a) there is a finite F ⊆ X0 which is m-dense(n,k), i.e. every coloring into k' ≤ min(k, min F) colors of [F]^{n'} has a homogeneous subset that is (m-1)-dense. 0-density means relatively large (|F| > min F). ItPH = ∀m mPH.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to rΠ^1_1-correctness of various theories and to well-foundedness of ordinals: PH^2 ↔ ItPH^2_2 ↔ WO(ω^ω) ↔ rΠ^1_1-corr(IΣ^0_1) ↔ rΠ^1_1-corr(WKL0+RT^2_2) (Thm 3.2); PH^3 ↔ ItPH^2 ↔ WO(ω^ω^ω) ↔ rΠ^1_1-corr(WKL0+RT^2) (Thm 3.3); PH ↔ ItPH^n_k for n ≥ 3 ↔ rΠ^1_1-corr(ACA0) ↔ WO(ε0) (Thm 3.5); ItPH ↔ rΠ^1_1-corr(ACA0') (Thm 3.6). First-order: PH ↔ Π2-corr(PA) over IΣ1 (Thm 2.1). WKL0+RT^n_k proves mPH^n_k → m+1PH^n_k (Prop 3.1).

statement.name: Generalized Paris–Harrington principle
statement.definition: For every largeness notion L and infinite set X0 there is a finite F ⊆ X0 that is m-dense(n,k,L).
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to FIRT^n_k, to RWKL^n_k, and to RT^n_k + RWKL^{n-}_k (Thm 4.5); equivalent to ACA0 for n ≥ 3. GPH ↔ RT ↔ Π^1_2-corr(ACA0) over RCA0 (Thm 4.7). ItGPH ↔ Π^1_2-corr(ACA0') (Thm 4.8). ItGPH^2_k ↔ rΠ^1_2-corr(WKL0+RT^2_k) over WKL0 for k = 2 or ∞ (Thm 4.6). Open whether ItGPH^2_2 is equivalent to RT^2 over WKL0 and whether ACA0 implies ItGPH^2.

statement.name: Finitary infinite Ramsey theorem
statement.definition: For every asymptotically stable f: [N]^{<N} → N there is r such that every coloring c: [[0,r)]^n → k has a homogeneous H ⊆ [0,r) with |H| > f(H).
statement.facts: Equivalent to RT^n_k over WKL0 (Gaspar/Kohlenbach, Pelupessy) and to GPH^n_k over RCA0 (Thm 4.5). The related FIPP3 is equivalent to ACA0 (unpublished note [45]).

statement.name: Ramsey-type weak König's lemma for (n,k)-coloring trees
statement.definition: RWKL^{n-}_k: every infinite (n,k)-coloring tree has an infinite homogeneous function. RWKL^n_k: it has a constant infinite homogeneous function. RWKL^1_2 is Flood's original RWKL.
statement.facts: RWKL^n_k ↔ RT^n_k + RWKL^{n-}_k over RCA0 (Thm 4.5); RWKL^1_2 is not provable in RCA0 and equals RWKL^{1-}_2. RWKL^{n-}_k is implied by WKL0; it is not known whether it is strictly weaker than WKL for n ≥ 2.

statement.name: Weak Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem on 2
statement.definition: WBWT2 : 2^N ⇒ 2^N maps p to the sequences q whose limit is a cluster point of p.
statement.facts: WBWT2 ≤W C̄_N, and WBWT2 ≰W C_N and ≰W L. It is strongly complete and not co-complete.

statement.name: Connected choice, positive connected choice and choice on Cantor space
statement.definition: Closed choice restricted to connected sets, to connected sets of positive measure, and choice on Cantor space.
statement.facts: C_{2^N} and CC[0,1] are complete, co-complete and co-total. PC_{2^N} and PCC[0,1] are co-complete, co-total and not complete. PCC[0,1] ≰W PC_R and PCC[0,1] ≰W C_N. PCC[0,1] is a strong total fractal. PC_{2^N} <W its completion ≤W TPC_{2^N} <W C_{2^N}, and TPC_{2^N} ≤W PC″_{2^N}. Cited: PC_{2^N} ≡sW WWKL.

statement.name: Infinity problem, negligibility problem and Sierpiński variants
statement.definition: INF decides whether a sequence has infinitely many zeros. NEG decides whether a closed subset of 2^N is null. The subscript S denotes target space the Sierpiński space.
statement.facts: LPO′ ≡sW INF ≡sW NEG and LPO′_S ≡sW INF_S. LPO′ and INF are co-total, and LPO′_S is co-complete but not co-total. LPO′_S ≤W TC_N and LPO′_S ≰W C_N.

statement.name: Low map
statement.definition: L := J^{-1} ∘ lim, and L2 := J^{-1} ∘ J^{-1} ∘ lim ∘ lim. A problem is low iff it is ≤sW L.
statement.facts: C̄_N is low2 but not low. L <sW L̄ and L is not a cylinder. L̄ is not complete. WBWT2, C̄_N and SORT are not ≤W L.

statement.name: Well-founded tree problems
statement.definition: The characteristic function of the empty closed set in A^-(N^N), with target {0,1} for WFT or Sierpiński space for WFT_S.
statement.facts: WFT′ ≡sW WFT. WFT and WFT_S are strongly complete and co-complete, and WFT is co-total. WFT_S ≤W TC_{N^N}, WFT_S ≰W C̄_{N^N}, and WFT_S is not co-total.

statement.name: Dense upwards-closed choice for Σ¹₁ sets
statement.definition: Given a non-empty quasi-order and a Σ¹₁-code for a dense upwards-closed subset A, find some element of A.
statement.facts: 1BS ≤W Σ¹₁-DUCC (Prop 5.1). It is equivalent to its restriction to (2^<N, ⊑) (Lemma 5.2). Fin_k(Σ¹₁-DUCC) ≡W RT^1_k (Thm 5.3). Det(Σ¹₁-DUCC) ≡W C_N (Prop 5.8).

statement.name: Π⁰₂ all-or-co-unique choice
statement.definition: Given a Π⁰₂ subset A of k (resp. N) missing at most one element, return an element of A.
statement.facts: Π⁰₂-ACC_2 ≡W RT^1_2. Π⁰₂-ACC_N ≰W lim (Prop 7.3). Fin_k of the parallelization of Π⁰₂-ACC_{k+2} is id (Cor 7.6). Fin_2(Π⁰₂-ACC_3 diamond) ≡W C_2 (Cor 7.10). The parallelization of Π⁰₂-ACC_2 is equivalent to KL (Fig. 2).

statement.name: Bad sequences restricted to trees; extendible vertex
statement.definition: BS|Tree: given a tree of infinite width, find an infinite antichain. ExtVer: given a tree of infinite width, find a vertex extendible to an infinite antichain.
statement.facts: BS|Tree ≤W the parallelization of Π⁰₂-ACC_k for every k≥2 (Prop 8.2). Fin_k(BS|Tree) ≡W id and Det(BS|Tree) ≡W id (Cor 8.3). ExtVer ≡W 1BS|Tree (Prop 8.5). Π⁰₂-ACC_N <W ExtVer <W the meet of the Π⁰₂-ACC_k (Cor 8.9). ACC_N × ACC_N ≰W BS|Tree (Cor 8.10). Whether BS|Tree ≤W DS is open (Question 8.11).

statement.name: Enumerating non-empty countable closed subsets of 2^N
statement.definition: Given a non-empty countable closed subset of 2^N, enumerate all its elements (possibly with repetition).
statement.facts: wList_{2^N,≤ω} ≰W BS and hence ≰W DS (Cor 4.6). It is parallelizable and lim ≤W wList_{2^N,≤ω}, cited from [19].

statement.name: Cofinitely-eventually correct descending/bad sequence
statement.definition: Given an ill-founded linear order (resp. non-well quasi-order), compute a sequence that is cofinitely a descending (resp. bad) sequence.
statement.facts: RT^1_2 × DS_FE ≤W DS and RT^1_2 × BS_FE ≤W BS (Prop 9.7). They are characterized as C_N → DS and C_N → BS.

items.quote: dN ≡W lim′ follows from Theorem 7.12

statement.name: Stable Ramsey theorem restricted to unbalanced colourings
statement.definition: SRT^2_k restricted to colourings such that all infinite homogeneous sets have the same colour.
statement.facts: TC_N, Sort and LPO' are each ≤_W u-SRT^2_2. u-SRT^2_k ≤_W lim' (indeed ≤_W lim_k ∗ lim). C_ℓ'' ≰_W u-SRT^2_k, so 1 u-SRT^2_k <_W 1 SRT^2_k.

statement.name: Fixed point theorem for positive Σ^0_k operators (Weihrauch problem)
statement.definition: Input: a set A and a Gödel number of an X-positive Σ^0_k formula ϕ(n,X,Y). Output: a fixed point of X ↦ {n : ϕ(n,X,A)}.
statement.facts: FP(Σ^0_2) ≡W MFP(Σ^0_2) (monotone Σ^0_2 operators, Corollary 3.4). FP(Σ^0_2) is parallelizable (Corollary 3.5). ATR2 ≤W FP(Σ^0_2) (Theorem 3.6, essentially Avigad). FP(Σ^0_2) is not Weihrauch reducible to ATR2 (Theorem 3.10), so ATR2 <W FP(Σ^0_2). Over RCA0 it is equivalent to ATR0 (Theorem 2.21, Avigad/Bärtschi, cited).

statement.name: Fixed point theorem for monotone Σ^0_2 operators
statement.definition: Input: a set A and a Gödel number of a Σ^0_2 formula ϕ such that X ↦ {n : ϕ(n,X,A)} is monotone. Output: a fixed point of that operator.
statement.facts: Weihrauch equivalent to FP(Σ^0_2), hence parallelizable.

statement.name: Δ^0_k-relativized leftmost path principle
statement.definition: Input: an ill-founded tree T ⊆ ω^<ω and a path f of it. Output: a path g of T such that no Δ^0_k(T⊕f⊕g) path h of T satisfies h <_l g.
statement.facts: Equivalent to the variant without the input path f in the output condition (Lemma 6.5). Δ^0_k β-model reflection ≤W Δ^0_k LPP (Lemma 6.8, from Towsner). (ATR2+Π^1_1-TI)^rfn ≤W Δ^0_3 LPP (Theorem 6.10). (Δ^0_n LPP+Π^1_1-TI)^rfn ≤W Δ^0_{n+2} LPP and (Δ^0_n LPP)^(k-rfn) <W Δ^0_{n+2} LPP (Theorem 6.12). Δ^0_k LPP ≤W Δ^0_k LFP(Π^0_1) (Theorem 7.6). Δ^0_k LCP(Σ^0_2) ≤W Δ^0_k LPP (Theorem 7.13). Δ^0_k LCP(Π^0_1) ≡W Δ^0_k LCP(Σ^0_2) ≡W Δ^0_k LPP (Corollary 7.14).

statement.name: Relativized least fixed point / least closed point theorems
statement.definition: Input: a set A and a Gödel number of an X-positive Σ^0_j formula. Output: a fixed point (resp. closed point) X such that no Σ^0_i(A⊕X)-definable fixed point (resp. closed point) Y is a proper subset of X.
statement.facts: Δ^0_k LFP(Π^0_{k'}) ≤W Δ^0_k LCP(Π^0_{k'}) for k'<k (Theorem 7.9). For k=2, Δ^0_k LPP ≡W Δ^0_k LFP(Π^0_1). For k≥3, Δ^0_k LPP ≡W Δ^0_k LFP(Π^0_1) ≡W Δ^0_k LFP(Σ^0_2) (Corollary 7.14). Σ^0_k LFP(Σ^0_1) is equivalent to lim (Remark 7.8).

statement.name: Σ^1_1 choice on sets
statement.definition: Input: a Σ^1_1 formula ϕ(X,Y) and a set A with ∃Xϕ(X,A). Output: a set B with ϕ(B,A).
statement.facts: Weihrauch equivalent to C_{ω^ω} (Lemma 4.15, d'Auriac). Any (Σ^1_∞,Σ^0_1)-representable problem is ≤W C_{ω^ω}, and (Π^1_1,Σ^0_1)-representable ones are <W C_{ω^ω} (Theorem 4.16).

statement.name: Minimum of a closed subset of ω+1 with negative information
statement.definition: The single-valued function min^-_{ω+1} :⊆ A^-(ω+1) → ω+1 maps a nonempty negatively represented closed A ⊆ ω+1 to min(A), where ω+1 = {-2^{-n}} ∪ {0}.
statement.facts: Proposition 3.1: Sort ≡_sW min^-_{ω+1}. Proposition 3.4: min^-_{ω+1} ≰_W BWT_n for every n ≥ 1. C_N ≡_W min^-_N ≤_sW min^-_{ω+1}.

statement.name: Exact projection operators onto closed subsets of R^n (negative, positive, total information)
statement.definition: Multi-valued functions mapping x ∈ R^n and a nonempty closed A ⊆ R^n (negative, positive or total representation) to the points of A closest to x.
statement.facts: Proj^- and Proj^+ ≤_sW BWT_R (Theorem 4.7). Proj^-_{R^n} ≡_sW BWT_R for n ≥ 2 (Corollary 4.9) and Proj^+_{R^n} ≡_sW BWT_R for n ≥ 2 (Corollary 4.15). Proj^-_R ≡_W BWT_2 × lim (Corollary 4.13) and Proj^+_R ≡_W BWT_2 × lim (Corollary 4.18). Proj_R ≡_W LLPO (Corollary 4.21), with LLPO ≤_sW Proj_R. Proj_{R^n} ≡_sW WKL for n ≥ 2 (Corollary 4.23). C_X ≤_sW Proj^-_X (Fact 4.3). The compact-set versions are equivalent to the closed-set versions in several cases (Theorem 4.6).

statement.name: Approximate projection operators onto closed subsets of R^n
statement.definition: Multi-valued functions returning points y of A with d(x,y) ≤ (1+ε) d(x,A), for A with negative, positive or total information.
statement.facts: ε-Proj^-_{R^n} ≡_sW C_R for all ε > 0 and n ≥ 1 (Theorem 5.4). ε-Proj^+_{R^n} ≡_W Sort for all ε > 0 and n ≥ 1 (Corollary 5.8). Hence the negative and positive versions are Weihrauch incomparable (Corollary 5.9). ε-Proj_{R^n} is computable (Theorem 5.10). The compact negative version satisfies WKL ≤_sW ε-Proj K^-_{R^n} ≤_W WKL * LPO^* * LPO <_W C_R (Proposition 5.5).

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass operators on {0,...,n-1} and unique-accumulation-point restrictions
statement.definition: BWT_n is BWT_X for X = {0,...,n-1}. UBWT_X is BWT_X restricted to sequences with compact range and a unique accumulation point.
statement.facts: Used in Proposition 3.4: min^-_{ω+1} ≰_W BWT_n; cited facts C_N ≡_W UBWT_N [BGM12, Cor. 11.24] and BWT_2 ≡_sW LLPO' [BGM12, Cor. 11.11].

statement.name: Cohesiveness relative to ∅'
statement.definition: COH relativized to ∅': every uniformly ∅'-computable sequence of sets has a cohesive set.

statement.name: Ramsey's theorem on general domains
statement.definition: Instances are pairs ⟨X, c⟩ with X an infinite set and c : [X]^n → k; solutions are infinite homogeneous subsets of X.
statement.facts: RT^n_k ≡W General-RT^n_k for all n, k ≥ 1 (Proposition 8.3.4(1)), and RCA0 proves ∀n∀k [RT^n_k ↔ General-RT^n_k].

statement.name: Paper's 2-RAN (Definition 3.6)
statement.definition: For every sequence of uniformly Π⁰₂ binary trees T_n with µ([T_n]) > 1 − 2^{-n}, there are n and X with X ∈ [T_n]. This is not the catalogue ran2.
statement.facts: RCA0 ⊢ 2-RAN ⇒ SAC (Proposition 3.7). Slaman (unpublished) proved that 2-RAN does not imply BΣ⁰₂ over RCA0.

statement.name: Infinite set with semi-heredity for some color
statement.definition: For any 2-coloring of pairs there is an infinite set which is semi-hereditary for some color.
statement.facts: It implies ADS over RCA0 and over computable reduction. It implies RT²₂ over RCA0. It is unknown whether RT²₂ is computably reducible to it (Question 8.4).

statement.name: CAC for stable trees
statement.definition: CAC restricted to stable (c.e.) trees, where a tree is stable if every node has either almost all nodes incomparable to it or almost all comparable to it.
statement.facts: SADS implies CAC for stable c.e. trees over RCA0 (Proposition 7.3). CAC for stable c.e. trees admits low solutions (Corollary 7.5). CAC for stable trees implies ∀k RT¹_k, and it is equivalent to CAC for stable c.e. trees and to SHER for stable colorings over RCA0 (Lemma 7.6, Corollary 7.9).

statement.name: Bolzano–Weierstraß theorem on a computable metric space X
statement.definition: BWT_X(x_n) is the set of cluster points of a sequence (x_n) in X with relatively compact range. Only the case X = R is in the catalogue (bwt).
statement.facts: BWT_X ≡sW K_X′ (Theorem 11.2). BWT_X ≡sW BWT_{0,1}^N for rich spaces X, so BWT_{R^n} ≡sW BWT_{l2} ≡sW BWT_[0,1] ≡sW BWT_{0,1}^N ≡sW BWT_{N^N}. BWT_2 ≡sW LLPO′ and BWT_N ≡sW (LLPO*)′. BWT_n <W BWT_{n+1} <W BWT_N <W BWT_R (Theorem 13.4). BWT_N is idempotent. BWT_2 ≰W lim.

statement.name: Cluster point problem and its unique version
statement.definition: CL_X = C_X ∘ L_X: given a sequence in X that has a cluster point, find a cluster point. UCL_X is the restriction to sequences with a unique cluster point.
statement.facts: C_X′ ≡sW CL_X (Theorem 9.4). CL_{N^N} ≡sW C_{N^N} (Theorem 9.16). BWT_R <W CL_R. UCL_R and CL_N are incomparable with BWT_R (Theorem 12.4). CL_R ≤sW L′ (uniform relative low basis theorem). Every computable sequence with a cluster point has a cluster point that is low relative to the halting problem.

statement.name: Unique Bolzano–Weierstraß theorem
statement.definition: The restriction of BWT_X to sequences with a unique cluster point.
statement.facts: UBWT_X = lim_X for Hausdorff X (Proposition 11.21). UBWT_R ≡sW lim and UBWT_N ≡sW C_N (Corollaries 11.22 and 11.24).

statement.name: Antithesis of Specker's theorem
statement.definition: Given a sequence of reals eventually bounded away from every point of [0,1], find N and k such that |x_n − x| > 2^{-k} for all x in [0,1] and n ≥ N.
statement.facts: AS ≡W C_N ≡W BCT (Theorem 15.2).

statement.name: Compact choice
statement.definition: K_X chooses a point from a nonempty compact set given with negative compact information (κ−). KC_X is C_X restricted to nonempty compact sets.
statement.facts: K_N ≡sW LLPO*. K_N <W KC_N ≡sW C_N. K_X ≡sW KC_X ≡sW C_X for computably compact X. K_X ≡sW K_{0,1}^N for rich X. K_R ≡sW C_{0,1}^N ≡sW WKL.

statement.name: Large Ramsey Theorem (Ramsey's theorem for exactly ω-large sets, the Schreier barrier)
statement.definition: For every k-coloring of the exactly ω-large finite sets (|s| = 1 + min s), there is an infinite homogeneous set.
statement.facts: Computable instances have ∅^(ω)-computable solutions (cited from Carlucci–Zdanowski and Clote). Some computable 2-coloring has all solutions computing ∅^(ω). RT^{!ω}_2 is equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.2). It implies FS^{!ω} over RCA0 (Corollary 3.5). Open: whether RT^{!ω}_2 ≤sW TS^{!ω} or ≤sW FS^{!ω}.

statement.name: Large Free Set Theorem
statement.definition: For every f : [N]^{!ω} → N there is an infinite H such that f(s) ∉ H \ s for all s ∈ [H]^{!ω}.
statement.facts: FS^{!ω} ≤sW RT^{!ω}_2 (Theorem 3.4). TS^{!ω} ≤sW FS^{!ω} (Theorem 3.7). RRT^{!ω}_2 ≤sW FS^{!ω} (Proposition 3.11). There is a computable instance all of whose free sets compute ∅^(ω) (Corollary 4.7). FS^{!ω} implies ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Corollary 4.8).

statement.name: Large Thin Set Theorem
statement.definition: For every f : [N]^{!ω} → N there is an infinite H with f([H]^{!ω}) ≠ N.
statement.facts: There is a computable coloring such that every infinite thin set uniformly computes ∅^(ω) (Theorem 4.6). It implies ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Corollary 4.8). TS^{!ω} ≤sW FS^{!ω} (Theorem 3.7). TS^{!ω} is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to the version omitting infinitely many colors (Proposition 3.8). TS^{!ω} ≤sW RRT^{!(ω+1)}_2 (Proposition 4.11).

statement.name: Large Rainbow Ramsey Theorem
statement.definition: For every k-bounded f : [N]^{!ω} → N there is an infinite H on which f is injective on [H]^{!ω}.
statement.facts: RRT^{!ω}_k ≤sW RT^{!ω}_k, and this is provable in RCA0 (Theorem 3.10). RRT^{!ω}_2 ≤sW FS^{!ω} (Proposition 3.11). It implies RRT^n_k over RCA0, with RRT^n_k ≤sW RRT^{!ω}_k (Proposition 3.12). There is a computable 2-bounded instance with no arithmetical solution (Theorem 4.10). It admits strong cone avoidance (Corollary 6.28), so it does not code ∅′ and does not imply ACA0. Open: whether RRT^{!ω}_k ≤sW FS^{!ω} for all k.

statement.name: Generalized Rainbow Ramsey Theorem for a barrier B
statement.definition: For every k-bounded coloring f : B → N, B ⊆ [N]^{<ω}, there is an infinite f-rainbow.
statement.facts: For computable barriers of order type ω^ω and k = 2, some computable instance has all rainbows computing ∅′ (Proposition 5.10). For computably ω-bounded barriers it admits strong cone avoidance (Corollary 6.28).

statement.name: Progressive Free Set Theorem (b-constrained progressive colorings into finite subsets)
statement.definition: For every b-constrained progressive coloring f : B → [N]^{<ω} there is an infinite f-free set.
statement.facts: For B = [N]^{≤h(·)} with h computable it admits strong cone avoidance (Theorem 6.14), strong PA avoidance and other notions of avoidance (Remark 6.27). For some computable barrier of order type ω^ω it does not admit cone avoidance (Proposition 6.13). With a non-computable bound b it does not admit strong cone avoidance (Proposition 6.26).

statement.name: k-Constrained Free Set Theorem
statement.definition: For every f : B → [N]^{≤k} there is an infinite f-free set.
statement.facts: FS^{≤n}_k admits strong cone avoidance (Proposition 6.8). FS^{≤!ω}_1 has a computable instance all of whose free sets compute ∅^(ω) (Corollary 4.7). Without the constant bound the statement is false (Proposition 6.9).

statement.name: Thin Set Theorem for finite colorings
statement.definition: For every coloring f : [N]^n → k there is an infinite set H thin for f, i.e. f([H]^n) ≠ k.
statement.facts: There is a uniformly computable family of colorings f_{n,k} : [N]^{n+k} → n such that every infinite thin set uniformly computes ∅^(k) (Lemma 4.5). A computable coloring [N]^{n+1} → n has every thin set computing ∅′ (Lemma 4.3).

statement.name: Valuation Extension Lemma
statement.definition: For every frame (W,R) and every assignment v : W × Prop → 2 there is a full Kripke valuation V : W × Fml → 2 on (W,R) extending v.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA+_0 (Theorem 2.5). Equivalent over RCA0 to ACA+_0 (Theorem 2.24). Implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Proposition 2.9). Corollary 2.13 gives a computable frame all of whose valuations compute ∅^(ω). Existence of some valuation on every frame is also equivalent to ACA+_0 (Theorem 2.24).

statement.name: Restricted Valuation Extension Lemma
statement.definition: For every frame, assignment v and k there is a k-restricted valuation (defined on formulas of modal degree ≤ k) extending v.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA'_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.25). Provable in ACA'_0 (Corollary 2.6). For standard k the k-restricted version is provable in ACA0 (Corollary 2.7). Existence of 1-restricted valuations on all frames is equivalent to ACA0 (Theorem 2.26).

statement.name: Frame definability for Geach axioms
statement.definition: For a frame F, the confluence-type first-order condition on iterated accessibility is equivalent to F validating Ga(i,j,m,n;φ) for all φ.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.24). The weak version, restricted to k-restricted valuations, is equivalent to ACA'_0 (Theorem 2.25).

statement.name: Frame definability for GL
statement.definition: F is transitive with no infinite R-ascending sequence iff F validates □(□φ→φ)→□φ for all φ.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.24). The weak version (3-restricted valuations) is equivalent to ACA0 (Theorem 2.26).

statement.notation: VEL, Geach and GL frame definability on image-finite frames
statement.name: Image-finite versions
statement.definition: VEL and the frame-definability principles for Geach axioms and GL, restricted to image-finite frames.
statement.facts: All are equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0. The finite-frame versions are provable in RCA0 (Corollary 2.28).

statement.notation: VEL for modal predicate logic; frame definability for BF and CBF
statement.name: Predicate modal logic VEL and Barcan formulas
statement.definition: VEL for variable-domain Kripke frames (W,R,D), and frame definability for the Barcan formula (domain-decreasing frames) and the Converse Barcan formula (domain-increasing frames).
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0, as is the existence of a valuation on every predicate frame (Theorem 2.34).

statement.notation: VEL for CTL, Restricted VEL for CTL, VEL for image-finite CTL
statement.name: Valuation Extension Lemma for CTL
statement.definition: VEL for CTL valuations on serial frames. The restricted version uses n-restricted valuations. The image-finite version is restricted to image-finite serial frames.
statement.facts: Restricted VEL for CTL implies Π^1_1-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.9) and is provable in Π^1_1-CA0 + Σ^1_2-induction (Theorem 3.10). VEL for CTL is provable in Σ^1_2-DC0 (Corollary 3.11). VEL for image-finite CTL is equivalent to ACA+_0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.15). Some CTL-valuation exists on every serial frame, provably in RCA0 (Theorem 3.16).

statement.name: Valuation Extension Lemma for LTL
statement.definition: For every LTL-frame (a single infinite path) and assignment v, there is an LTL-valuation extending v.
statement.facts: Implies ACA0 over RCA0 (Corollary 3.19) and is provable in ACA'_0 (Theorem 3.32). The restricted version is provable in ACA'_0 (Proposition 3.20). The exact strength is open (Questions 4.1 and 4.2).

statement.name: Strong cohesive principle
statement.definition: COH together with IPP; equivalently cohesiveness with finitely many exceptions uniformly bounded. This is not the catalogue's stcoh (COH restricted to stable sequences).
statement.facts: Equivalent to StCADS over RCA0 (Proposition 5.9, from Hirschfeldt–Shore). Π^0_3-conservative over RCA0, citing [19]. Strictly weaker than ADS [19]. RT^2_2 and StCOH, even together with WKL, are Π^0_4-conservative over RCA0+IPP. Equivalent over RCA0 to Heine–Borel (Thm 5.15), Bolzano–Weierstrass (Thm 7.9), Arzelà–Ascoli (Thm 7.18), and to boundedness, uniform continuity and attainment of extrema for continuous functions on [0,1] (Thm 6.1), and to every bounded sequence of rationals having a Cauchy subsequence (Lemma 5.13, Kreuzer).

statement.name: Co-finite choice and its boundedness version
statement.definition: C_F is choice on non-empty co-finite subsets of N. B_F maps a left-c.e. real x to any upper bound in [x,∞).
statement.facts: B_F ≡sW C_F ≡W C_N (Proposition 3.3). C_N ≡W B_F is idempotent and is reduced to by LPO.

statement.name: Interval choice, proper interval choice and boundedness versions
statement.definition: Choice on non-empty closed intervals of [0,1] (C_I), on proper closed intervals (C_I^-), and the boundedness versions with sup q_n ≤ x ≤ inf r_n. B_I^+ allows r_n = ∞.
statement.facts: B_I ≡sW C_I and B_I^- ≡sW C_I^- (Proposition 3.6). IVT ≡sW C_I (Theorem 6.2). The chain LLPO < C_I^- < C_I < C_K ≡ WKL is strict, C_I^- < C_N, and C_N | C_I. C_I^- ≤W C_N, and C_I is not reducible to C_I^-.

statement.name: Compact choice
statement.definition: Choice on non-empty compact subsets of a computable metric space.
statement.facts: C_K(X) ≤sW LLPO^, with equality when {0,1}^N embeds computably into X (Theorem 2.10). C_K ≡W WKL, and HBT ≡W C_K (Theorem 7.1).

statement.name: Countable closed choice (the map A ↦ characteristic function of A)
statement.definition: The map taking a negative-information name of A ⊆ N to its characteristic function.
statement.facts: B ≡W C ≡W LPO^ (Proposition 3.7). C_A <W C (Proposition 4.8).

statement.name: Baire Category, Banach Inverse Mapping, Open Mapping, Closed Graph and Uniform Boundedness theorems as multi-valued operations
statement.definition: The realizers of these classical theorems on computable complete metric spaces and Banach spaces.
statement.facts: BCT_X ≡W C_N for any non-empty complete computable metric space X, and UBT_{X,Y} ≡W C_N for Banach spaces different from {0}. IMT, OMT and CGT are ≤W C_N, with equivalence on ℓ2.

statement.name: Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem and Weierstraß Approximation Theorem as operations
statement.definition: The realizers of BFT and WAT as multi-valued operations.
statement.facts: BFT ≤W WKL (Corollary 8.7) and computable fixed points have low names (Corollary 8.8). WAT ≡W id (Corollary 8.4).

statement.name: Iterated jump AST
statement.facts: AST(0) ≡ AST. AST(n) → AST(m) for m<n over RCA0 (Prop 4.3). AST(m) is the weakest natural principle failing in every ω-model of low_m sets. AST(m) is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA0. DNR(m) → AST(m) over RCA0. AST(n) does not hold in every ω-model of WKL(m) for m<n (Thm 4.6). Over RCA0, WKL(m) + ¬IΣ⁰_{m+1} → AST(n) (Kolodziejczyk, personal communication).

statement.name: Iterated jump DNR
statement.definition: ∀X ∃Y Y^(m) is DNC over X^(m).
statement.facts: DNR(0) ≡ RWWKL, and DNR(1) ↔ Seq*(TS) over RCA0. WWKL(m) → DNR(m) and DNR(m) → AST(m) over RCA0. WWKL(m) ⇏ DNR(m) over ω-models (Thm 4.5). DNR(m) is not implied over ω-models by WKL(n) for m<n (Thm 4.7). Its first-order part is unknown.

statement.name: Iterated jump WWKL
statement.definition: ∀X ∃Y Y^(m) computes a 1-random over X^(m).
statement.facts: WWKL(0) ≡ WWKL. WKL(m) → WWKL(m) and WWKL(m) → DNR(m) over RCA0. WKL(m) is not implied by WWKL(m) over ω-models (Thm 4.4). RCA0* ⊢ WWKL(m) → BΣ⁰_{m+1} (Kolodziejczyk, using FCKWY24).

statement.name: Iterated jump WKL
statement.definition: ∀X ∃Y Y^(m) ≫ X^(m) (Y^(m) is of PA degree over X^(m)).
statement.facts: WKL(0) ≡ WKL, and WKL(1) ↔ COH over RCA0. ACA → WKL(m), and WKL(m) → WWKL(m) over RCA0. RCA0* ⊢ WKL(m) → BΣ⁰_{m+1}. WKL(m) is Π¹₁-conservative over RCA0* + BΣ⁰_{m+1}. The WKL(m) are logically independent over ω-models (Belanger). Thm 4.4: WKL(m) is not implied by WWKL(m) over ω-models. Thm 4.6: for m<n, AST(n) is not implied by WKL(m) over ω-models. Thm 4.7: for m<n, DNR(m) is not implied by WKL(n) over ω-models.

statement.name: Sequential thin set theorem for singletons with finite errors
statement.definition: For every sequence ⟨f_i⟩ of functions N→N there is an infinite H such that for each i some H_i =* H has f_i(H_i) ≠ N.
statement.facts: ω-models of Seq*(TS1) are those I where each X ∈ I has Y ∈ I with Y′ DNC over X′ (Thm 2.17, cited). Equivalent to DNR(1). COH → Seq*(TS1) and RRT22 → Seq*(TS1) over RCA0; Seq*(TS1) → AST over RCA0. Seq*(TS1) is not implied by WKL, FIP or OPT over ω-models, and COH is not implied by it. New result Prop 3.2: RCA0 ⊢ Seq*(TS1) → OPT, strengthening COH → OPT and RRT22 → OPT.

statement.name: Hausdorff dimension of closed subsets of [0,1] (resp. as upper real)
statement.definition: The map A ↦ dim_H(A) from closed subsets of [0,1] to R, and the variant dim_H^> with output type R>.
statement.facts: dim_H ≡W lim ⋆ lim and dim_H^> ≡W lim (Theorem 48). Corollary 53: there is a computable closed and computably overt set whose Hausdorff dimension is Turing-equivalent to ∅''.

statement.name: Maximal flow on the infinite binary tree
statement.definition: Given a non-negative edge assignment f on the full binary tree, find a flow g ≤ f with g(ε) maximal.
statement.facts: MaxFlow ≡W lim.

statement.name: Non-zero flow
statement.definition: Given an edge assignment f, find a flow g ≤ f with g(ε) > 0.
statement.facts: NonZeroFlow ≡W C_N × C_{0,1}^N (≡ C_N × WKL) (Theorem 39), which is ≡W C_R (Corollary 57).

statement.name: Construct a measure supported in a closed set
statement.definition: Given a non-empty closed A ⊆ X, find a non-zero measure µ with supp(µ) ⊆ A.
statement.facts: ConstructMeasure_X ≡W C_X for a computable Polish space X (Theorem 34). ConstructMeasure[0,1] <W supp^{-1} (Corollary 35). ConstructMeasure[0,1] ≡W C[0,1] ≡W H1 C[0,1] (Figure 1).

statement.name: Support of a measure and inverse
statement.definition: supp maps a measure to its support (as overt set, or as closed set); supp^{-1} constructs a measure with a given closed set as support.
statement.facts: supp : M(X) → V(X) is computable. For X perfect (or with a computable embedding of N) and effectively locally compact, supp^A_X ≡W (supp^A_X)^{-1} ≡W lim (relative to the Halting problem otherwise).

statement.name: Frostman measure constructions
statement.definition: Given a closed A ⊆ [0,1] and s, find an s-Frostman measure supported in A (resp. with support exactly A).
statement.facts: Frost ≡W C_N × C[0,1] ≡W NonZeroFlow (Corollary 57); StrictFrost ≡W lim ≡W MaxFlow (Corollary 58).

statement.name: Closed choice on sets of positive Hausdorff dimension (resp. dimension 1)
statement.definition: Restriction of C[0,1] to closed sets of positive Hausdorff dimension, resp. dimension 1.
statement.facts: HC[0,1] ≡W H1 C[0,1] ≡W C[0,1] (via Shmerkin's construction).

statement.name: Perfect core and concentrated-measure operations
statement.definition: PerfectCore maps a closed set A to a closed and overt B ⊇ A with the same perfect kernel; Concentrate produces a concentrated non-atomic measure below a given one; ConcentratedSupport computes the support of a concentrated measure as closed and overt.
statement.facts: All three are computable.

statement.name: Upper bound for monotone bounded sequence of naturals
statement.definition: Given a monotone bounded sequence of naturals, find an upper bound.
statement.facts: Used to show WKL × UpperBound ≤W NonZeroFlow.

statement.name: (Induced) subgraph decision problems
statement.definition: For a computable graph G, IS_G(H)=1 iff G is isomorphic to an induced subgraph of H, and S_G(H)=1 iff G is isomorphic to a subgraph of H. The e-versions take graphs given by enumerations as input.
statement.facts: For finite G, LPO ≡sW S_G ≡sW IS_G, and for G not a complete graph LPO' ≡sW eIS_G (Theorem 3.17). For infinite c.e. G with R ⊑s G, or with K_ω not induced in G, the problems are ≡sW WF (Lemmas 3.18, 3.19), so there is no c.e. G with LPO <W IS_G <W WF (Theorem 3.20). For the trees T_{2k+1} and forests F_{2k+2}, S_G is ≡sW LPO^(2k) resp. LPO^(2k+1) (parallelized), by Theorem 3.22.

statement.name: (Induced) subgraph search problems
statement.definition: Given a graph H containing G as a (induced) subgraph, output a (induced) subgraph of H isomorphic to G. There are four variants (χχ, χe, eχ, ee) according to whether input and output graphs are given by characteristic function or by enumeration.
statement.facts: These problems are cylinders (Prop. 4.2) and are bounded above by C_NN (Prop. 4.3). IS-Copy_G ≡W C_NN, possibly relative to an oracle (Thm 4.5). S-Copy_G ≡W C_NN when G has only finitely many vertices of finite degree (Thm 4.6) and for G ∈ {L, C_n ⊔ R, K_m ⊔ R, 2^{<N}} (Prop. 4.14). S-Copy_G is computable for finite G (Thm 4.4) and for certain disjoint unions of finite graphs (Thm 4.39). IS-Copy of the disjoint union of all C_i (i≥3) is ≡W C_NN (Thm 4.40). S-Copy_R <W C_NN, and C_NN ≡W lim^2 ⋆ S-Copy_R (Cor. 4.16). S-Copy_R is incomparable with lim in some variants (Thm 4.18). The first-order part of S-Copy_R is that of C_NN (Prop. 4.17). S-Copy_{F_{2k+2}} ≤W the parallelization of LPO^(2k-1) (Thm 4.44).

statement.name: Ray embedding problem
statement.definition: Given a graph H isomorphic to G, where R ⊑s G, find a sequence p such that (p(i), p(i+1)) is an edge of H for every i.
statement.facts: These problems are cylinders (Prop. 4.11) and are ≤W C_NN (Lemma 4.12). R-Emb_R ≡W eR-Emb_R ≡W lim^2 (Prop. 4.15). R-Emb_G ⋆ S-Copy_R ≡W C_NN (Prop. 4.13).

statement.name: Strong Σ¹ₙ dependent choice
statement.definition: For η in Σ¹ₙ: ∃Z ∀n (∃Y η(n,(Z)<n,Y) → η(n,(Z)<n,(Z)n)).
statement.facts: Equivalent to Σ¹ₙ-Rfn over ACA0 (Thm 3.1).

statement.notation: Categoricity of DLO, random graph, atomless Boolean algebras
statement.name: Countable categoricity principles
statement.definition: Any two countable dense linear orders without endpoints (resp. random graphs, atomless Boolean algebras) are isomorphic, with the inverse isomorphism also existing.
statement.facts: Each is equivalent to RCA0 over PRA2.

statement.notation: IntermediateValueTheorem, Completeness of R, HeineBorelTheorem (problem forms)
statement.name: Problem forms of analysis theorems
statement.definition: Instances are presentations of functions, Cauchy sequences, or covers of [0,1] by rational open intervals. Solutions are a point where the function is discontinuous or zero, the limit, or an uncovered point.
statement.facts: Over PRA2, HeineBorelTheorem is equivalent to WKL0 (Proposition 6.5). IntermediateValueTheorem is conjectured to be equivalent to Δ⁰₁-CA over PRA2 (Proposition 5.8). For each of these, every computable instance has a primitive recursive instance whose solutions compute a solution (Theorem 5.4).

statement.name: Baer type problem
statement.definition: Given a Baer categorical rank 1 torsion-free abelian group, output its Baer type, i.e. the set {m : m | g} for a nonzero g.
statement.facts: Every c.e. degree is the degree of the solutions of some computable instance. The only primitive recursive instance is the trivial group (Proposition 5.11).

statement.notation: Szpilrajn, graph reorientation, Rival–Sands for honest graphs, Hall's theorem variants, connected components
statement.name: Combinatorial principles done in PRA2
statement.definition: Szpilrajn's theorem; transitive reorientation of pseudo-transitive oriented graphs; Rival–Sands and (2n-1)-colouring for honestly presented locally finite graphs; Hall's theorem for finite A or under the extended Hall condition; existence of connected components.
statement.facts: The first four are proved in PRA2 (Propositions 3.11–3.13). Existence of connected components, under the hypothesis that finitely many vertices have every vertex connected to one of them, is equivalent to 2^N-RCA0 over PRA2 (Proposition 3.14).

statement.name: Determinacy of finite differences of open sets on Cantor space
statement.definition: For every n, every Gale–Stewart game on {0,1} whose payoff is a (possibly nonstandard) n-fold difference of Σ⁰₁ sets is determined.
statement.facts: Over ACA0 it is equivalent to ACA'0 (Propositions 3, 4) and to Π¹₂-Ref(ACA0) (Theorem 15); in particular it is equivalent to a Π¹₂ sentence.

statement.name: Determinacy of finite differences of open sets on Baire space
statement.definition: For every n, every Gale–Stewart game on N whose payoff is an n-fold difference of Σ⁰₁ sets is determined.
statement.facts: Over ACA0 it is equivalent to Π¹₁-CA'0 and to Π¹₃-Ref(Π¹₁-CA0) (Theorem 12).

statement.name: Determinacy of finite differences of Σ⁰₂ sets
statement.definition: For every n, every Gale–Stewart game on N whose payoff is an n-fold difference of Σ⁰₂ sets is determined.
statement.facts: Over ACA0 it is equivalent to Π¹₃-Ref(Π¹₂-CA0) and to ∀n.[Σ¹₁]n-ID (Theorem 16). Over RCA0 it is equivalent to its Cantor-space version ∀n.(Σ⁰₂)n-Det* (Proposition 5).

statement.name: Determinacy of finite differences of Σ⁰₃ sets
statement.definition: For every n, every Gale–Stewart game on N whose payoff is an n-fold difference of Σ⁰₃ sets is determined.
statement.facts: Over ACA0 it is equivalent to Π¹₃-Ref(Z2) (Theorem 29). This uses Montalbán–Shore: Π¹ₘ₊₂-CA0 proves (Π⁰₃)m-Det, and (Π⁰₃)m-Det proves the existence of β-models of Δ¹ₘ-CA0.

statement.name: Π¹₁-CA0 with finite iterated hyperjumps
statement.definition: RCA0 plus: for all n and X there is a chain of coded β-models X ∈ X0 ∈ ... ∈ Xn with each model a β-submodel of the next (equivalently, HJ^n(X) exists).
statement.facts: Equivalent over ACA0 to ∀n.(Σ⁰₁)n-Det and to Π¹₃-Ref(Π¹₁-CA0) (Theorem 12).

statement.name: Iterated Σ¹₁ inductive definitions
statement.definition: The existence of sets inductively defined by combinations of k Σ¹₁ transfinite-induction operators.
statement.facts: Over ATR0, MedSalem–Tanaka show (Σ⁰₂)k-Det ↔ [Σ¹₁]k-ID. In this paper ∀n.(Σ⁰₂)n-Det implies ∀n.[Σ¹₁]n-ID over ATR0 (Proposition 7), and ∀n.[Σ¹₁]n-ID implies ∀n.ψ₁(2,n) over ACA0 (Lemma 18).

statement.name: Strong Σ¹ₖ dependent choice
statement.definition: ACA0 plus a scheme asserting ∃Z∀n∀Y.(η(n,(Z)_n,Y) → η(n,(Z)_n,(Z)^n)) for Σ¹ₖ formulas η.
statement.facts: Equivalent over ACA0 to Π¹ₖ-CA0 for k = 1, 2 (Simpson VII.6.9), and to the existence for every X of a βk-model containing X.

statement.name: Rival–Sands theorem for k-chain decomposable partial orders
statement.definition: Every infinite partial order that comes with a decomposition into k chains has a (0,∞)-homogeneous chain. RSpo^CD_<∞ is ∀k RSpo^CD_k.
statement.facts: RSpo^CD_3 → ADS (Lemma 6.1). RSpo^CD_2 ↔ SADS over RCA0 (Theorem 6.6(3)). RSpo^CD_<∞ → IΣ02 (Lemma 6.3). RSpo^CD_<∞ ↔ RSpo_<∞ ↔ IΣ02 + ADS over RCA0. RSpo_k ↔ RSpo^CD_k for k ≥ 3 over RCA0 (Theorem 6.6(2)). RSpo_2 ↔ RSpo^CD_2 over WKL0.

statement.name: Rival–Sands theorem with 'cofinitely many'
statement.definition: Every infinite partial order of width ≤ k (resp. k-chain decomposable) has a (0,cof)-homogeneous chain, that is, every element is comparable with none or with cofinitely many elements of the chain.
statement.facts: (0,cof)-RSpo_2, (0,cof)-RSpo^CD_2 and ADS are pairwise equivalent over RCA0 + IΣ02 (Theorem 6.6(5)). Π^1_1-CA0 proves (0,cof)-RSpo_<∞ (Theorem 4.10). (0,cof)-RSpo^CD_2 → ADS (Lemma 6.4). The exact strength of (0,cof)-RSpo_<∞ is open (Question 6.7).

statement.name: Infinite chain for partial orders of bounded width; infinite antichain for partial orders of bounded height
statement.definition: CC_k: every infinite partial order of width ≤ k has an infinite chain. CA_k: every infinite partial order of height ≤ k has an infinite antichain.
statement.facts: RCA0 proves CC_k and CA_k for each fixed standard k (Proposition 3.8). CC_<∞, CA_<∞ and BΣ02 are pairwise equivalent over RCA0.

statement.name: n-stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs
statement.definition: RT^2_k restricted to k-colorings of pairs such that for every x at most n values y > x have c(x,y) ≠ c(x,y+1).
statement.facts: RCA0 proves n-stable SRT^2_k for fixed standard n and k. For fixed n, BΣ02 ↔ n-stable SRT^2_<∞ over RCA0, and IΣ02 ↔ ∀n (n-stable SRT^2_<∞) over RCA0 (Proposition 5.8).

statement.notation: Rival–Sands for partial orders without infinite antichains
statement.name: Extension of Rival–Sands to partial orders with no infinite antichain
statement.definition: Every infinite partial order with no infinite antichain has a (0,∞)- (resp. (0,cof)-) homogeneous chain.
statement.facts: The (0,∞) version is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0, and equivalent to the version for well-partial-orders (Theorem 7.8). Π^1_1-CA0 proves the (0,cof) version (Theorem 7.2). The exact strength of the (0,cof) version is open (Question 7.9).
