statement.name: k-colorability of locally k-colorable graphs
statement.definition: Every locally k-colorable graph is k-colorable.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 for every k ≥ 2 (Hirst, cited).

statement.name: Σ⁰ₙ relative leftmost path principle
statement.definition: Every ill-founded tree T ⊆ N^{<N} has a Σ⁰ₙ-leftmost path, i.e. a path f that is lexicographically least among the paths of T that are Σ⁰ₙ in T ⊕ f. Definition 4.3 gives a Weihrauch-problem version (input T and a path f, output a Σ⁰ₙ-leftmost path g).
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to ∆⁰ₙ LPP (Lemma 3.4), and Weihrauch equivalent to ∆⁰ₙ LPP (Lemma 4.4). For k>1 (Theorem 3.28) it is equivalent over RCA0 to R∆⁰ₖ β-RFN, to the ω-model reflection of Π¹ₖ₊₁-TI, and to the ω-model reflection of ∆⁰ₖ(Π¹₁)-TI. It is equivalent to RFN(Π¹ₖ₊₂-RFN0) (Corollary 3.31). Σ⁰ₙ₊₁ LPP proves the ω-model reflection of Σ⁰ₙ LPP, hence is strictly stronger than Σ⁰ₙ LPP over RCA0 (Corollary 3.32). In the Weihrauch lattice, Σ⁰ₙ LPP ≡W R∆⁰ₙ βRFN for n>1 (Theorem 4.5), and Σ⁰ₙ LPP <W Σ⁰ₙ₊₁ LPP for n>0 (Theorem 4.8).

statement.name: Arithmetic leftmost path principle
statement.definition: Every ill-founded tree has a Σ⁰ω-leftmost path.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, ALPP is equivalent to β⁰₁RFN(1), to RFN(Π¹∞-TI) and to RFN(AΠ¹₁-TI) (Theorem 3.13). The equivalence with the single pseudo hyperjump is attributed to [6], and the equivalence with RFN(Π¹∞-TI) to Freund [1].

statement.name: ∆⁰ₖ leftmost path principle
statement.definition: Every ill-founded tree has a path f that is lexicographically least among {g ∈ [T] : g ≤_T TJ^{k-1}(T ⊕ f)}.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to Σ⁰ₖ LPP (Lemma 3.4), and Weihrauch equivalent to Σ⁰ₖ LPP (Lemma 4.4). It follows from RFN(∆⁰ₖ(Π¹₁)-TI0) over RCA0 (Lemma 3.27).

statement.name: Colorability of locally ℓ-colorable graphs with k colors
statement.definition: COL(ℓ,k,G) says: if G is a locally ℓ-colorable graph then G is k-colorable. The two principles quantify k uniformly over G and non-uniformly, respectively.
statement.facts: Theorem 5.2 (cited from Hirst), 5.3 (Gasarch–Hirst) and 5.4 (Schmerl): for fixed standard k ≥ ℓ ≥ 2, WKL is equivalent over RCA0 to every locally ℓ-colorable graph being k-colorable. Theorem 5.7: ∀ℓ∃k∀G COL+BΣ02 does not prove WKL. Theorem 5.8: ∀ℓ∀G∃k COL+BΣ02 does not prove ∃k∀f DNR(k,f). Proposition 6.1: RCA0+BΣ02 does not prove ∀k(∀f DNR(k,f) → ∀G COL(k,2k−1,G)).

statement.name: Prediction statement of Schmerl
statement.definition: There is an X with Σ01(X)-definable sets N=D0⊇...⊇Dn and Σ01(X)-definable functions Hi: Di+1→k such that every family of Σ01(Y)-definable functions Fj: Dj→k agrees with the Hi at some common point x in Dn.
statement.facts: Predict_1(k) essentially says ∃f ¬DNR(k,f). Proposition 6.8: if Predict_n(k) holds and Adam has a winning strategy in the on-line coloring game, then some graph in the natural class is not k-colorable. Corollary 6.11: Predict_{f(k)}(k) implies there is a locally 2-colorable graph that is not k-colorable.

statement.name: Radical-maximal implies primary
statement.definition: If the radical of I exists and is maximal, then I is primary (equivalently, if I is not primary and its radical exists, then the radical is not maximal).
statement.facts: Provable in WKL0 (Proposition 4.11) and provable in RCA0 plus WKL0, but exact strength open (Question 4.13); lies between RCA0 and WKL0.

statement.name: Radical maximal implies primary for all ideals
statement.definition: For all ideals I of R, if the radical of I is maximal then I is primary.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0.

statement.name: Four notions of Noetherian ring
statement.definition: Σ1-Noetherian: every Σ1-ideal finitely generated; ∆1-Noetherian: every ∆1-ideal finitely generated; ∆1-a.c.c.: ascending chains of ∆1-ideals stabilise; sequentially Noetherian: no sequence a_i with a_i not in (a_0..a_{i-1}).
statement.facts: Σ1-Noeth implies ∆1-Noeth, sequential Noeth, ∆1-a.c.c. over RCA0; sequential Noeth implies ∆1-a.c.c. Theorem 5.4: RCA0+IΣ2 proves equivalence of weak and strict chain conditions for Σ1-ideals. Theorem 5.10: ACA0 equivalent to 'every ring with ∆1-a.c.c. is Σ1-Noetherian' (also with ∆1-Noetherian or sequentially Noetherian variants). Theorem 5.11: WKL0 equivalent to 'every ring with ∆1-a.c.c. is sequentially Noetherian'. Corollary 5.13: WKL0 equivalent to 'every Artinian ring is sequentially Noetherian'.

statement.name: Ascending chain condition on principal ideals
statement.definition: No strictly increasing chain of principal ideals; two formulations equivalent over RCA0+IΣ2.
statement.facts: Σ1-Noetherian rings have a.c.c.p.; Theorem 6.23 (cited, Bura/Greenberg–Melnikov): ACA0 equivalent to 'in a ring with a.c.c.p. every element has an irreducible factorisation'.

statement.name: Classes of integral domains
statement.definition: Σ1-PIDs, UFDs, Bézout domains and GCD domains.
statement.facts: Euclidean domains are PIDs and DHD implies PID in RCA0; every GCD domain is AP in RCA0; ACA0 proves PIDs are UFDs; Theorem 6.26: in ACA0, if every prime Σ1-ideal is principal then R is a PID; Theorem 6.44: RCA0+IΣ3 proves R UFD implies R[x] UFD; Theorem 6.41 RCA0: R field iff R[x] Euclidean iff R[x] PID.

statement.name: Dedekind–Hasse domain norm statement
statement.definition: Every PID admits a Dedekind–Hasse norm.
statement.facts: Provable in ACA0 and implies ACA0 over RCA0, hence equivalent. Corollary 6.38: ACA0 equivalent to 'for any PID the set of units exists' and to 'the set of primes exists'. Theorem 6.39: computable PID whose set of irreducibles is Π2 complete.

statement.name: Arithmetical Zorn's lemma
statement.definition: For Γ subset A of N and Θ partial order on N, if every chain has an upper bound then (A,≼) has a maximal element.
statement.facts: ACA0 proves ZL(arithmetical, arithmetical); RCA0 proves ZL(Σ1,Σ1) (Theorem B.4); ZL(Γ,Θ) is equivalent to ACA0 if Γ contains Π1 and ≤ is Θ, or N is Γ and Θ contains Π1 (Corollary B.6).

items.quote: BCT1 ≡sW CN ≤sW PCN×2N ≤sW WWKL′ by [12, Theorem 9.3] and by Fact 1.4
items.concerns: The reduction goes through PC_{N×2^N}, which is not in the catalogue.
reasons: attributed by the paper to [12, Theorem 9.3]: cite the original

statement.name: Limit operation with respect to the jump topology
statement.definition: lim restricted to sequences that converge in the jump topology.
statement.facts: BCT_0′ ≤sW lim_J, and BCT_0′ <W lim_J. lim_J is not probabilistic (Corollary 9.8).

items.quote: although J ≡sW EC by Fact 1.10.
reasons: attributed by the paper to Fact 1.10 ([BG11b]): cite the original

items.quote: DNCN <sW DNCn+1 <sW DNCn
items.argument: Take n = 2 in Fact 5.5(1): DNC_N <sW DNC_3.
reasons: attributed by the paper to Jockusch 1989 [Joc89, Theorem 6]: cite the original

statement.name: Range non-equality problem
statement.definition: Given p, find A ∈ 2^N with A ≠ range(p−1).
statement.facts: NRNG ≡sW DIS (Corollary 5.12 / Proposition 1.13).

statement.name: Non-majorization problem
statement.definition: Given ⟨i,p⟩, find q ∈ N^N with ϕ_i^p(n) ≱ q(n) for some n. An asymmetric version of DIS.
statement.facts: DIS <W NMAJ <W HYP (Proposition 6.3). NMAJ-hat ≡sW HYP. The stashing of NMAJ is ≡W DIS, so NMAJ is not stashable. It is open whether the stashing of NMAJ is ≡sW DIS (Question 6.4). NMAJ ≰W DIS.

statement.name: Non-greater-or-equal problem
statement.definition: Given ⟨⟨i,n⟩,p⟩, find k ∈ N with ϕ_i^p(n) ≱ k.
statement.facts: DIS ≤sW NMAJ ≤sW NGEQ ≤W LPO. The stashing of NGEQ is ≡W DIS (Proposition 6.3).

statement.name: Meeting principle
statement.definition: Given p, find q ∈ N^N such that for every r ≤_T p there is n with r(n) = q(n) (introduced by Hölzl, Raghavan, Stephan and Zhang).
statement.facts: HYP ≡W MEET (Proposition 6.6); HYP ≤sW MEET, but the reverse reduction is not strong.

statement.name: Retraction and extension problems
statement.definition: RET_X(x) = {y ∈ X : x ∈ X ⇒ x = y}, a multi-valued retraction from the completion of X onto X. EXT_Y gives total extensions of partial functions with range in Y.
statement.facts: RET_X-hat ≡sW EXT_X (Corollary 7.5). LLPO ≤sW RET_n ≡sW AUC_n ≤sW C_n and RET_n ≤sW RET_N ≡W LPO (Proposition 7.8). RET_n-hat ≡sW WKL, and the stashing of RET_n and RET_N is ≡W DIS (Corollary 7.9). RET_X ≤sW lim for totally represented X and RET_N ≤sW C_N (Fact 7.7).

statement.name: All-or-unique choice on {0,…,n−1}
statement.definition: X \ range(p−1) for X = n, restricted to inputs where the set is the whole of n or a singleton. AUC_2 = LLPO.
statement.facts: AUC_n <W AUC_{n+1} <W AUC_N for n ≥ 2 (Proposition 7.10). AUC_n ≡sW RET_n. AUC_n is not equal to the catalogue's auc, which is on [0,1].

statement.name: All-or-co-unique choice on n
statement.definition: X \ range(p−1) restricted to inputs with |range(p−1)| ≤ 1, for X = n ≥ 3; ACC_2 = LLPO and ACC_N is accn.
statement.facts: ACC_N <sW ACC_{n+1} <sW ACC_n for n ≥ 2 (Weihrauch 1992). ACC_n-hat ≡sW DNC_n. The stashing of ACC_n is ≡sW DIS (Proposition 5.6).

statement.name: Discontinuity problem with n values
statement.definition: DIS_n(p) = {q ∈ n^N : U_n(p) ≠ q} for a truncated universal function U_n.
statement.facts: ACC_n-stashed ≡sW DIS_n ≡sW DIS for all n ≥ 2 (Proposition 5.6).

statement.name: Limit avoidance and non-lowness problems
statement.definition: NLIM_N: given a convergent sequence in N^N, find k ≠ its limit. NLOW: given a, find b with b' ≰ a'.
statement.facts: ACC_N ≤sW NLIM_N ≤sW NLIM_2 ≡sW lim_2 ≤sW lim_N ≡sW C_N (Fact 8.2). The stashing of NLIM_N is not ≤W WKL (Proposition 8.3), so DIS is not its stashing: the phase transition lies between LPO and lim_2. ΠΣ(NLIM_N) ≤sW NLOW (Proposition 8.4), and NLOW is parallelizable.

statement.name: Atsuji spaces (every continuous function on the space is uniformly continuous)
statement.definition: A complete separable metric space A is Atsuji if every continuous function from A to an arbitrary complete separable metric space B is uniformly continuous.
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0: every Lebesgue space is Atsuji (Thm 6.1). Provable in ACA0: every Atsuji space is Lebesgue (Thm 6.7); the paper does not know whether ACA0 is needed. Over WKL0, ACA0 is equivalent to 'every perfect Atsuji space is compact' (Thm 4.3). Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to 'every compact space is Atsuji' and to '[0,1] is Atsuji' (Thm 4.1), and also to 'there exists a perfect Atsuji space' (Lemma 4.5). Heine-Borel compact spaces are Atsuji in RCA0 (Lemma 4.2).

statement.name: Lebesgue spaces (every open covering has a Lebesgue number)
statement.definition: A complete separable metric space A is Lebesgue if for every open covering U of A there is q>0 such that every ball B(x,q) is contained in some member of U.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to '[0,1] is Lebesgue' (Thm 5.5). Heine-Borel compact spaces are Lebesgue in RCA0 (Lemma 5.3). Every perfect Lebesgue space is Heine-Borel compact in RCA0 (Thm 5.4). Over WKL0, ACA0 is equivalent to 'every perfect Lebesgue space is compact' (Thm 5.6). Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to 'there exists a perfect Lebesgue space' (Lemma 5.7).

statement.name: Compactness notions in weak subsystems
statement.definition: Compact: there is a sequence of finite 2^-n-nets of the space. Heine-Borel compact: every open covering has a finite subcovering.
statement.facts: Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to 'every compact space is Heine-Borel compact' (Thm 3.4, Brown/Simpson). Over WKL0, ACA0 is equivalent to 'every Heine-Borel compact space is compact' and also to the version restricted to perfect spaces (Thm 3.6). Over RCA0, WKL0 is equivalent to 'there is a perfect Heine-Borel compact space' (Lemma 3.8).

statement.name: Continuity of the distance function from a closed set
statement.definition: For every closed set C there is a continuous function f_C(x)=inf{d(x,y): y in C}; variants say that {(x,e): B(x,e) is not contained in U} is open.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to Π¹₁-CA0 (Thm 7.1). The version for separably closed sets is equivalent to ACA0 (Thm 7.3).

statement.name: Closed versus separably closed sets (Brown)
statement.definition: A separably closed set is the closure of a coded sequence of points; a closed set is the complement of a coded open set.
statement.facts: Cited from Brown: over RCA0, ACA0 is equivalent to 'every separably closed set is closed'. Π¹₁-CA0 is equivalent to 'every closed set is separably closed'.

statement.name: Countable Zorn's lemma (three forms)
statement.definition: For a nonempty countable poset in which every linearly ordered subset is bounded above: ZL-1, every element lies below a maximal element; ZL-2, the set of maximal elements exists (is nonempty); ZL-3, there is a function assigning to each element a maximal element above it.
statement.facts: ZL-1 is provable in RCA0 (Theorem 2.2). ZL-2 and ZL-3 are each equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 2.3).

statement.notation: P IP for D_n, D̄_n (n ≥ 3), and F
statement.name: Intersection-property maximality principles (general family)
statement.definition: Every nontrivial family of sets has a ⊆-maximal subfamily with the D_n (any n distinct sets have empty intersection), D̄_n (any n distinct sets have nonempty intersection) or F (finite intersection) property. Only n = 2 and the F version have catalogue entries.
statement.facts: All are provable in ACA0. D_n IP is equivalent to ACA0 for each n. F IP implies D̄_n IP. D̄_{n+1} IP implies D̄_n IP. Whether these implications are strict is open (Question 5.1). The strong-subfamily variants (Proposition 3.8) are equivalent to ACA0.

statement.name: Finite character principle (and restrictions)
statement.definition: For each formula φ of finite character, every set A has a ⊆-maximal subset B with φ(B). Γ-FCP restricts it to formulas in a class Γ.
statement.facts: Γ-FCP is provable in Γ-CA0, and reverses to Γ-CA0 for Γ = Π^0_n, Π^1_n, Σ^1_n, Δ^1_n (Theorem 4.4). Σ^0_1-FCP and QF-FCP are provable in RCA0 (Proposition 4.7). Π^0_n-FCP is equivalent to ACA0, Π^1_n-FCP and Σ^1_n-FCP to Π^1_n-CA0, and full FCP to Z2 (Corollary 4.6). A sequential form of Σ^0_1-FCP is equivalent to ACA0 (Proposition 4.8).

statement.name: Maximal extension with finitary closure operator
statement.definition: For a finitary closure operator D, a formula φ of finite character and a set A, every D-closed subset of A satisfying φ is contained in a maximal such subset.
statement.facts: Γ-CE is provable in Γ-CA0 (Theorem 4.12). QF-CE, Σ^0_0-CE and Σ^0_1-CE are each equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Proposition 4.13, Corollary 4.14). Full CE is equivalent to Z2.

statement.name: Maximal extension with nondeterministic finitary closure operator
statement.definition: Like CE, but the closure operator is nondeterministic: a set is N-closed if, whenever F ⊆ A, A meets S for each pair ⟨F,S⟩ in N.
statement.facts: Σ^1_1-NCE, Σ^0_n-NCE (n ≥ 1) and QF-NCE are each equivalent to Π^1_1-CA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 4.21). Σ^1_n-NCE and Π^1_n-NCE are provable in Π^1_n-CA0, and Δ^1_n-NCE in Δ^1_n-CA0 (Proposition 4.22). Corollary 4.23 gives the corresponding equivalences, and full NCE is equivalent to Z2. Π^0_2-NCE implies that every ideal on a countable poset extends to a maximal ideal (Proposition 4.19).

statement.name: Milliken's theorem for sums / unions
statement.definition: The sum version MT: for every n and every finite partition of [N]^n there is an infinite X that is homogeneous on the sums-of-blocks collection <X>^n. MTU is the union version for finite sets.
statement.facts: MT ↔ MTU over RCA0 (Lemma 7.21). MT is equivalent to the strong Hindman theorem of Theorem 7.5 over RCA0 (Theorem 7.22). ACA0' proves MT (Corollary 7.23). RCA0 ⊢ MT → ACA0 (Corollary 7.24). Theorem 7.25 characterises MT in countable models via additive restricted Galvin ultrafilters.

statement.name: Algebraic Hindman theorem
statement.definition: For every finite partition of an infinite Boolean ring R there is an infinite subring that is monochromatic.
statement.facts: Equivalent to HT over RCA0 (Theorem 7.8). It cannot be extended to all rings, to rings of finite characteristic, or to monochromatic ideals (Theorems 7.9–7.11). Equivalent to the Boolean-algebra version (Theorem 7.12) and to a version with a monochromatic subring isomorphic to R for Boolean rings of finite sets (Porism 7.13).

statement.name: Infinite marriage theorems (Hall) and symmetric/bounded versions
statement.definition: Marriage problems in which each boy knows finitely many girls and condition H holds have solutions (the symmetric versions have symmetric solutions); the bounded versions add a bounding function.
statement.facts: The unbounded versions are equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0, and the bounded versions (including k-societies) to WKL0 (Theorems 2.2, 2.3, 3.1, 3.3). The finite marriage theorem is provable in RCA0 (Theorem 2.1).

statement.name: Countable bounded Banach theorem
statement.definition: For injections f,g:N→N whose ranges exist there is a bijection h with h(n)=m implying f(n)=m or g(m)=n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.5). The version without range hypotheses is equivalent to ACA0 (Theorem 3.8).

statement.name: Rado's selection principle (thesis formulation) and weak version
statement.definition: Choice-function principles for families of finite subsets of N coded by pairs or finite-set codes, with a weak version using a bounding function.
statement.facts: The principle is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.30) and the weak version to WKL0 (Theorem 3.31). The formulation differs from the catalogue's rado, so it was not matched.

statement.name: Dimension bound for n pairwise incomparable chains
statement.definition: For each poset P and pairwise incomparable chains C_i ⊆ P (i<n), dim(P) ≤ dim(P \ ∪C_i) + max{2,n}.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 for every n≥1; likewise ∀n DB^i_n is equivalent to WKL0 (Theorems 4.4, 4.7, 4.10, Corollary 4.8). DB^i_1 and DB^i_2 are due to Hiraguchi, and the bounds are sharp (Examples 3.1–3.3).

statement.name: Dimension bound for n arbitrary chains
statement.definition: For each poset P and chains C_i ⊆ P (i<n), dim(P) ≤ dim(P \ ∪C_i) + 2n.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 for each n, and ∀n DB^c_n is equivalent to WKL0 (Theorems 4.6, 4.7, 4.9). The bound is sharp (Example 3.5). DB^c_1 coincides with DB^i_1.

statement.name: Dimension bound for removing a point
statement.definition: For each poset P and x_0 ∈ P, dim(P) ≤ dim(P \ {x_0}) + 1.
statement.facts: Provable in WKL0 and also in IΣ^0_2, so it is equivalent to neither (Corollary 5.6). It follows from LS* over RCA0 (Corollary 5.4).

statement.name: Strong dimension bound for removing a point
statement.definition: For each poset P and x_0 ∈ P, if (L_j)_{j<n} realizes P \ {x_0}, then there is a realization (L'_j)_{j<n+1} of P with L_j = L'_j restricted to P \ {x_0} for j<n-1.
statement.facts: Equivalent to LS* over RCA0 (Theorem 5.3). Provable from WKL0 and from IΣ^0_2. Not provable in RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 (Corollary 5.9).

statement.name: Linear separation principle
statement.definition: For each linear order L and sets I, F ⊆ L with I below F, there is a separator set B (an initial interval containing I and disjoint from F).
statement.facts: Provable in RCA0 (Lemma 5.2) but with no uniform proof, since it relies on non-uniform information. As a problem it is Weihrauch equivalent to XC_1, the restriction of closed choice on [0,1] to convex sets (Proposition A.1), and so it is not computable.

statement.name: Finite parallelization of LS
statement.definition: For each k and each finite sequence (L_j, I_j, F_j)_{j<k} of linear orders with I_j below F_j, there is a sequence (B_j)_{j<k} of separator sets.
statement.facts: Equivalent to DB_p^+ over RCA0 (Theorem 5.3). Provable from WKL0 and from IΣ^0_2 (Corollary 5.6) but implies neither. The statement "LS* is computably true" is equivalent to IΣ^0_2 over RCA0 (Corollary 5.9). RCA0 + BΣ^0_2 does not prove LS* (Corollary 5.9).

statement.name: Closed choice on [0,1] restricted to convex (interval) sets
statement.definition: Given a nonempty closed convex subset A of [0,1], presented by rational open intervals covering its complement, find a point of A.
statement.facts: Weihrauch equivalent to LS (Proposition A.1, proved by Arno Pauly). Its degree was studied in Le Roux–Pauly and Kihara–Pauly.

items.quote: Again, it is easy to see that WKL♦ ≡W WKL ≡W jvO (see e.g. [18, Proposition 4.9]).
reasons: attributed by the paper to [18] Hirschfeldt–Jockusch, Proposition 4.9: cite the original

statement.name: Weak König's lemma for 2-trees
statement.definition: WKL restricted to 2-trees (binary trees with exactly two strings at each length); Weihrauch equivalent to C_{2^ω,#≤2}; constructively equivalent to the binary expansion principle BE.
statement.facts: (WKL≤2)♦ ≡W (WKL≤2)* (Fact 5.2, from Le Roux–Pauly/Pauly–Tsuiki). WKLaou ≰cW (WKL≤2)♦ (Prop. 5.3). WKLclop → WKLaou (Prop. 4.2). WKL≤2 ≰cW F for F with a semicontinuous bound, in particular WKL≤2 ≰cW (RT12 × Limω)♦ (Prop. 5.9). WKLconv ≰cW (RT12 × Limω × WKL≤2)♦ (Prop. 5.10). WKL≤2 ≰cW (WKL=2 × WKLaou)♦ and WKL≤2 ≰cW (WKLclop)♦.

statement.name: Weak König's lemma for rational 2-trees
statement.definition: WKL≤2 restricted to rational 2-trees (2-trees with finitely many branching nodes).
statement.facts: BEQ ↔ WKL=2 (Prop. 4.5). WKLclop → WKL=2 (Prop. 4.3). WKL=2 ≰cW (WKLaou)♦ (Prop. 5.5). WKL=2 ≤W Limω.

statement.name: Weak König's lemma for all-or-unique trees
statement.definition: WKL restricted to binary trees that at each length have either all strings or exactly one string. Weihrauch equivalent to the all-or-unique choice AoUC and to robust division RDIV.
statement.facts: (WKLaou)♦ ≡W (WKLaou)* ⋆ (WKLaou)* (Fact 5.4, from Kihara–Pauly). WKLaou ≰cW (WKL≤2)♦ (Prop. 5.3). WKL=2 ≰cW (WKLaou)♦ (Prop. 5.5). LLPO ≤W WKLaou is used in the proof of Lemma 5.12.

statement.name: Weak König's lemma for convex trees
statement.definition: WKL restricted to convex binary trees; equivalent to IVT.
statement.facts: WKLconv ≰cW (RT12 × Limω × WKL≤2)♦ (Prop. 5.10). IVT ≰cgW Σ02-DML × Σ02-DNE × BE (Thm 5.1(5)).

statement.name: Weak König's lemma for convex clopen trees
statement.definition: WKLconv restricted to convex clopen trees.
statement.facts: IVTlin ↔ WKLclop (Prop. 4.6). WKLclop → WKLaou, WKLclop → WKL=2 (Props. 4.2, 4.3). Σ02-DNE → WKLclop (Prop. 4.4). WKLclop ≰cW (WKLaou × WKL≤2)♦ (Prop. 5.7). WKLclop ≤W Limω.

statement.name: Binary expansion principle
statement.definition: Every regular Cauchy real has a binary expansion; equivalent over EL0 to WKL≤2.
statement.facts: RDIV ≰cgW BE; BE ≰cgW Σ02-DML × Σ02-DNE (Thm 5.1). Used to separate IVT, BE, RDIV, LLPO over IZF via realizability (Thm 1.1).

statement.name: Binary expansion for regular Cauchy rationals
statement.definition: If a regular Cauchy real happens to be rational (non-irrational), then it has a binary expansion.
statement.facts: BEQ ↔ WKL=2 (Prop. 4.5). BEQ ≰cgW RDIV (Thm 5.1(2)).

statement.name: Intermediate value theorem for piecewise linear maps
statement.definition: IVT restricted to continuous functions that are rational piecewise linear maps as a discrete limit.
statement.facts: IVTlin ↔ WKLclop (Prop. 4.6). IVTlin ≰cgW RDIV × BE (Thm 5.1(3)).

statement.name: de Morgan's law for Σ02 formulas on the reals
statement.definition: ¬(φ ∧ ψ) → ¬φ ∨ ¬ψ for Σ02 formulas with real parameters, viewed as a multifunction.
statement.facts: Σ02-DML_R ≡W RT12 (Prop. 4.8). BE ≰cgW Σ02-DML × Σ02-DNE (Thm 5.1(4)).

statement.name: Double negation elimination for Σ02 formulas / discrete limit
statement.definition: Σ02-DNE as a multifunction; Limω is the limit operation on discrete ω (returns the eventual value of a sequence of naturals that stabilizes).
statement.facts: Σ02-DNE_R ≡W Limω (Prop. 4.7). Limω does not satisfy rCT! (Example 3.38). Limω <W Limω! ≡W lim_{ω^ω}.

statement.name: Robust division principle
statement.definition: For all x,y in [0,1] with x ≤ y there is z in [0,1] with x = yz; Weihrauch equivalent to AoUC.
statement.facts: Realizability separations over IZF between RDIV, BE, IVT, WKL, LLPO (Thm 1.1); RDIV ≰cgW BE (Thm 5.1(1)).

statement.name: Jordan decomposition on rationals (without continuity)
statement.definition: For every (continuous) function f of bounded variation there are nondecreasing functions g,h defined on I_Q = Q∩[0,1] with f = g − h on I_Q.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WKL0 over RCA0 (Theorem 7.4); computably, B is PA-complete iff for each computable bounded-variation f, B computes g: I_Q→R with f ≤slope g (Theorem 7.3); strong Jordan_Q also equivalent to WKL0.

statement.name: Differentiability of BV functions (pseudo-differentiable point)
statement.definition: Every continuous bounded variation function f:[0,1]→R has a pseudo-differentiable point; aeBVDiff says it is pseudo-differentiable almost surely.
statement.facts: Equivalent to WWKL0 over RCA0 with aeBVDiff (Theorem 8.1); provable within WWKL0 (Proposition 8.2); existence of a derivative somewhere is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0 (Rute, Remark 8.5).

statement.name: Randomness existence principles C0 = RCA0 + ∀X∃Y[Y ∈ C^X]
statement.definition: RCA0 plus the statement that for each X there is a Y that is ML-random / computably random / Schnorr random relative to X.
statement.facts: CR0 does not imply MLR0 (ω-model, Proposition 9.1); CR0 is equivalent to SR0 (Proposition 9.2); MLR0 is equivalent to WWKL at least for ω-models; MLR0 and DiffR0 expected equivalent.

statement.name: Every continuous bounded variation function has a variation function
statement.definition: Every continuous function of bounded variation has a variation function V_f.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0.

statement.name: (Weak) Paris–Harrington principles for pairs
statement.definition: Existence of 1-large (weakly) homogeneous sets for k-colorings of pairs from sparse sets, relativized or bounded by Fh.
statement.facts: Over RCA0*: WPH^{h,2}_k = k-HCT^h = k-TT^h = k-HCT^h_b = k-TT^h_b, and PH^{h,2}_k = k-HCT^h_H = k-TT^h_H. Each WPH*^2_k is equivalent to RCA0 over RCA0*. ∀k WPH*^2_k = ∀k k-TT*_ω = ∀k Tot*(F_k) = ∀k PH*^2_k over RCA0. Corollary 8.8: relations bounded by F_h with k of them have a bound F_{k+h+5}.

statement.notation: k-HCT^h, k-TT^h, k-HCT_ω, k-TT*_ω and bounded/H-bounded variants
statement.name: Bounded versions of the H-closure and Termination Theorems
statement.definition: H-closure and Termination Theorems restricted to relations of height ω (with weight functions) or with bounds or H-bounds, with growth conditions via the fast-growing hierarchy.
statement.facts: Equivalent level by level to WPH or PH as listed in Theorems 7.1–7.3. Used to show that a relation bounded by F_k has a (k+2)-disjunctive transition invariant of F_0-bounded relations (Theorems 8.9, 8.10).

statement.name: Iterated (weak) Paris–Harrington principles
statement.definition: Existence of m-w-dense (resp. m-dense) sets above any a, for 2-colorings of pairs.
statement.facts: mWPH^2_2 is provable in WKL0 + CAC, so WW_m is primitive recursive. HH_m is provably recursive in WKL0 + RT^2_2 and bounds all such functions (Bovykin–Weiermann), and is primitive recursive by the Patey–Yokoyama conservation result.

statement.name: Layer function for a universal Martin-Löf test
statement.definition: LAY_U : MLR ⇒ N with n ∈ LAY_U(p) iff p ∉ U_n; its degree does not depend on the universal test U.
statement.facts: LAY ≡W RD ≡W C_N × d_MLR (Theorem 3.3). LAY×LAY ≡W LAY and LAY⋆LAY ≡W LAY (Cor. 3.4). LAY <W C_N (Cor. 3.5). LAY⋆C_N ≡W C_N⋆LAY ≡W LAY (Cor. 3.6). LAY <W LAY-hat ≡W lim × d_MLR (Cor. 3.7). LAY <W LAY* ≡W id ⊔ LAY <W C_N (Cor. 3.8). A function f is ≤W LAY iff it is effectively Δ⁰₂-measurable iff Π⁰₁-piecewise computable (Cor. 3.10). Every layerwise computable f satisfies f ≤W LAY (Obs. 3.2).

statement.name: Randomness deficiency function
statement.definition: RD_U : MLR → N, RD_U(p) = min{n : p ∉ U_n}.
statement.facts: RD ≡W LAY ≡W C_N × d_MLR (Theorem 3.3).

statement.name: Kolmogorov randomness deficiency
statement.definition: Kol(p) = min{c : ∀n K(p≤n) ≥ n − c}, for p ∈ MLR.
statement.facts: Kol ≡W C_N × d_MLR (Proposition 3.11).

statement.name: Law of the iterated logarithm (effective, multivalued)
statement.definition: LIL : MLR ⇒ N with N ∈ LIL(α) iff for all n ≥ N, |Σ_{i<n}(2α(i)−1)| < sqrt(2n log log n).
statement.facts: LIL ≡W LAY (Theorem 4.8).

statement.name: Toy Birkhoff theorem convergence rate
statement.definition: Birkhoff : MLR × N ⇒ N with N ∈ Birkhoff(p,k) iff for all n ≥ N the average of π1(S^i(p)) for i ≤ n differs from 1/2 by less than 2^{-k}.
statement.facts: Birkhoff ≡W LAY (Theorem 4.10). The general convergence rate in Birkhoff's ergodic theorem is not layerwise computable.

statement.name: Random harmonic series
statement.definition: The map sending p ∈ MLR to Σ_n (−1)^{p(n)}/n ∈ R.
statement.facts: It is layerwise computable (Dai) and ≡W LAY (Theorem 4.12).

statement.name: Approximate sum comparison for random harmonic series
statement.definition: SumApr : MLR × Q × N ⇒ {0,1} with 0 ∈ SumApr(p,q,k) if the random harmonic sum is < q + 2^{-k}, and 1 ∈ SumApr(p,q,k) if the sum is > q.
statement.facts: Layerwise computable, not computable, and not Weihrauch-complete for layerwise computability.

statement.name: Kleene star of LPO
statement.definition: LPO* is defined by f^0 = id, f^{n+1} = f^n × f, f*(n,x) = f^n(x), applied to LPO.
statement.facts: (min :⊆ A(N)→N) ≡W LPO* (cited from Mylatz [25]; the text writes O(N)). LPO* <W C_N even relative to any oracle (cited from [29]).

statement.name: Overt choice on a represented space X
statement.definition: VC_X :⊆ V(X) ⇒ X takes a non-empty closed set A, given by positive information about which open sets intersect it (an element of V(X)), and returns a point of A.
statement.facts: VC_X is computable for precomputable quasi-Polish X (Theorem 20). For countably-based T1 spaces, VC_X is continuous iff X is quasi-Polish (Corollary 23). For coanalytic separable metric spaces, VC_X is continuous iff X is Polish (Corollary 36). VC_X × VC_Y ≤sW VC_{X×Y} (Corollary 10). VC_X ≤W Π02 C_X' for a computable surjection X' → X (Proposition 31). For effectively countably-based X, any f :⊆ {0,1}^N ⇒ N with f ≤W VC_X is computable (Proposition 28). So C_N ≰W VC_X unless VC_X is computable (Corollary 30 for homogeneous spaces gives incomparability with C_N). Overt choice on a CoPolish space is continuous iff the space is countably-based. For Fréchet-Urysohn CoPolish X, VC_X ≤tW LPO (Theorem 60) and ACC_m ≰W VC_X (Theorem 63). For non-Fréchet-Urysohn T1 X, LPO ≤tW VC_X (Theorem 64), and VC_X ≤W (id: ΣΠ11 → Σ) for CoPolish X (Theorem 67). Corollary 68 gives a trichotomy for CoPolish spaces.

statement.name: Overt choice on the rationals
statement.definition: Overt choice VC_X for X = Q, the Euclidean rationals as a subspace of R.
statement.facts: VC_Q ≡W ECP (Proposition 39). It is not computable (Proposition 38). VC_Q |W C_N ≡W C_Q (Corollary 40). VC_Q ≰W C_R (Corollary 41). VC_Q ≡W VC_Q* (Corollary 35). HitSparse <W VC_Q (Corollary 44). Open: is it reducible to lim or to Sort?

statement.name: Overt choice on the space S0
statement.definition: Overt choice on S0, the set of finite sequences of naturals with the topology generated by the sets {u | u ⋠ w}.
statement.facts: FSL ≤W VC_S0 (Proposition 47). FSL <W VC_S0 (Corollary 48). VC_S0 ≡W VC_S0* (Corollary 35). Open: relation to VC_Q, lim and Sort.

statement.name: Overt choice on the CoPolish Fréchet-Urysohn space Tmin
statement.definition: Overt choice on the space Tmin with underlying set N^2 ∪ {∞}, a Fréchet-Urysohn CoPolish space that is not countably-based.
statement.facts: ACC_N ≤sW VC_Tmin (Proposition 57). Hence VC_Tmin is not computable or continuous.

statement.name: Overt choice on the CoPolish non-Fréchet-Urysohn space Smin
statement.definition: Overt choice on the space Smin on {(∞,∞)} ∪ (N×{∞}) ∪ N^2, a CoPolish space that is not Fréchet-Urysohn.
statement.facts: VC_Smin ≡W LPO (Theorem 66). The reduction LPO ≤sW VC_Smin is strong.

statement.name: Eventually constant path
statement.definition: Given an enumeration of a non-empty tree T ⊆ {0,1}* in which every vertex extends to an eventually constant path, find an eventually constant path.
statement.facts: ECP is not computable (Proposition 38). ECP ≡W VC_Q (Proposition 39).

statement.name: Finite sequence leaf
statement.definition: Given an enumeration of a non-empty tree with a leaf below every vertex, find a leaf, as an element of the space S{0,1}* of finite sequences.
statement.facts: FSL is not computable (Proposition 46). FSL ≤W VC_S0 and FSL ≤W C_N. FSL <W VC_S0.

statement.name: Hit sparse
statement.definition: Given an infinite A ⊆ N (as a closed set, by negative information) and f: N → N, find an open set U meeting A with |[n,f(n)] ∩ U| ≤ 1 for all n.
statement.facts: HitSparse is not computable, and HitSparse ≤W VC_Q (Theorem 43, due to Brattka). HitSparse ≤W C_N. HitSparse <W VC_Q (Corollary 44).

statement.name: Closed choice on the rationals
statement.definition: Closed choice C_X for X = Q.
statement.facts: C_Q ≡W C_N (Proposition 26). If f :⊆ X ⇒ Q satisfies f ≤W C_R then f ≤W C_N (Corollary 27).

statement.name: All-or-co-unique choice on {0,...,m-1}
statement.definition: ACC_m is the problem of finding an element of a closed set from {M, M \ {i} | i ∈ N}, where M = {0,...,m-1}.
statement.facts: ACC_2 ≡W LLPO. ACC_m ≰W VC_X for admissibly represented Fréchet-Urysohn X and m ≥ 2 (Theorem 63).

statement.notation: MLE restricted to disjoint unions of two linear orders
statement.name: MLE for I ⊕ J
statement.definition: MLE applied only to partial orders that are the disjoint union of two linear orders.
statement.facts: Equivalent over RCA0 to ATR0 and to MLE (Theorem 1.5); the reversal uses only such partial orders.

statement.name: Weak comparability of well-orders
statement.definition: If L0 and L1 are well-orders then L0 embeds into L1 or L1 embeds into L0.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Friedman–Hirst [FH90]). Also equivalent to the statement that any sequence of well-orders has i≠j with Li embeddable into Lj (Shore [Sho93]).

statement.name: Existence of Cantor normal forms
statement.definition: Every well-order is equivalent to a finite sum of ω-exponentials with nonincreasing exponents.
statement.facts: Equivalent to ATR0 over RCA0 (Hirst [Hir94, Theorem 5.2]).

statement.name: Rival–Sands theorem for graphs, refined
statement.definition: RSg with the extra requirement that every vertex of H has either infinitely many or no neighbours in H.
statement.facts: ACA0 proves it (Theorem 3.2). It is equivalent to RSg and ACA0 over RCA0 (Theorem 3.5). RSg ≤sW RSgr ≤sW 3-DNR2. RSgr ≡sW RSg ≡sW WKL'' (Corollary 6.12), so it is a cylinder. RSgr↾LF ≡sW lim.

statement.name: Weak Rival–Sands theorem for graphs, refined
statement.definition: An infinite H such that every v in H has either infinitely many or no neighbours in H.
statement.facts: RT^2_2 ↔ wRSgr over RCA0 (Theorem 3.6). wRSg ≤sW wRSgr and wRSg ≡c wRSgr (Proposition 7.4). It is open whether wRSgr ≤W wRSg (Question 7.5). SADC ≰W wRSgr (Theorem 7.7). DNR ≰W wRSgr (Theorem 7.8). SRT^2_2 ≤W LPO ∗ wRSgr (Theorem 7.14(1)). It has the same location in the Weihrauch degrees as wRSg (Theorem 7.11).

statement.notation: RSg for locally finite graphs (and its refined version)
statement.name: Rival–Sands theorem for locally finite graphs
statement.definition: RSg restricted to graphs in which each vertex has finitely many neighbours.
statement.facts: As a sentence it is equivalent to ACA0 over RCA0. RSg↾LF ≡sW RSgr↾LF ≡sW lim, so RSg↾LF <c RSg.

statement.name: Iterated 2-bounded DNR problems
statement.definition: (n+1)-DNR2: given p, output a 2-valued function that is DNR relative to p^(n); DNR2^(n) is the n-th jump of DNR2.
statement.facts: WKL^(n) ≡sW DNR2^(n) ≡sW (n+1)-DNR2, so WKL'' ≡sW 3-DNR2 (Lemma 4.13). 3-DNR2 ≡sW RSg (Corollary 6.12). WKL ≡sW DNR2 is cited from [5, Corollary 5.3].

statement.name: Omniscient COH
statement.definition: Given a sequence A of subsets of ω, output p in 2^ω such that A_{p↾n} is infinite for every n.
statement.facts: INForONE ≡W oCOH (Proposition 6.6). oCOH ≡sW WKL' (remark after Corollary 6.12). It is a cylinder (Lemma 6.11).

statement.name: Omniscient COH in Δ^0_2
statement.definition: Given a Δ^0_2-approximation to an infinite set Z and a sequence A, output p with Z ∩ A_{p↾n} infinite for every n.
statement.facts: 3-DNR2 ≤sW oCOH-in-Δ^0_2 (Lemma 6.8). It is equivalent to INForONE-in-Δ^0_2 and INForONE-in*-Δ^0_2 (Lemma 6.7). It is a cylinder, and is strongly Weihrauch equivalent to RSg and WKL'' (Corollary 6.12).

statement.name: Infinity-or-one problems
statement.definition: Given a sequence A of sets in which each x lies in only finitely many A_i, output an infinite D with |D ∩ A_i| = ω or ≤ 1 for each i. The Δ^0_2 versions restrict D to a Δ^0_2-approximated set Z, either exactly or modulo finite sets.
statement.facts: INForONE ≡W oCOH ≡sW WKL' and INForONE is not a cylinder. INForONE-in*-Δ^0_2 ≤sW RSg (Lemma 6.9). The Δ^0_2 versions are cylinders and strongly equivalent to RSg and WKL'' (Corollary 6.12).

statement.name: Restrictions of the Rival–Sands problems to graphs with vertex set ω
statement.definition: The problems restricted to input graphs with V = ω.
statement.facts: RSg↾V=ω ≡sW RSg. wRSg↾V=ω ≡W wRSg but is strictly below it in ≤sW and is not a cylinder (Proposition 7.2). wRSg ≡sW id × wRSg↾V=ω.

statement.name: CADS with strictly stable suborders
statement.definition: CADS where the solution must have order type ω, ω*, or ω+ω*.
statement.facts: CADS^strict ≰W CADS, so CADS <W CADS^strict.

statement.name: Extension Auslander-Ellis theorem
statement.definition: Given a compact system (X1,T1) with points x1,y1 satisfying the conclusion of AET and a second system (X2,T2) with x2, there is y2 such that (y1,y2) is uniformly recurrent and proximal to (x1,x2) in the product system.
statement.facts: Follows from adaptations of classical proofs of AET; implies eAET'; strength unknown (Question 1). ACA_0^omega+(mu)+(Umin) proves eAET'; ACA_0^omega+(mu)+IHT+(Umin) is Pi^1_2-conservative over ACA_0+eAET; eAET proves that every finite partition of a central set contains a central set.

statement.name: Refinement eAET' of the Auslander-Ellis theorem
statement.definition: For each n and each sequence of continuous i-ary functions t_i : X^i -> X (i<n), there is (y_i)_{i<n} uniformly recurrent in the n-fold product and proximal to (t_0, t_1(y_0), ..., t_{n-1}(y_0,...,y_{n-2})).
statement.facts: Implied by eAET; ACA_0^omega+(mu)+(Umin) proves eAET' (Theorem 16); ACA_0^omega+(mu)+IHT+(Umin) is Pi^1_2-conservative over ACA_0+eAET' (Corollary 15); strength unknown.

statement.notation: partial minimal idempotent ultrafilter for countable algebras
statement.name: Existence of partial minimal idempotent ultrafilters on countable algebras
statement.definition: For every countable (downward translation) algebra there is a partial non-principal ultrafilter F satisfying idempotency (*) and minimality (†).
statement.facts: For arbitrary countable algebras, existence of partial non-principal (resp. minimal) ultrafilters is equivalent to ACA_0 over RCA_0. For downward translation algebras, existence of partial minimal idempotent ultrafilters, of partial idempotent ultrafilters, and of almost downward translation invariant ultrafilters are each equivalent to AET and IHT over ACA_0.

statement.name: Existence of a minimal idempotent ultrafilter (higher-order)
statement.definition: There is a higher-order object U of type 2 that is a non-principal, idempotent, minimal ultrafilter on N, respecting coding of sets.
statement.facts: ACA_0^omega+(mu)+IHT+(Umin) is Pi^1_2-conservative over ACA_0+eAET (Theorem 14); the statement forall f exists U minimal idempotent extending tF(f) proves eAET over ACA_0^omega+(mu) (Theorem 18).

statement.name: Every real belongs to a countable Scott set
statement.definition: The assertion, formalized in second-order arithmetic, that every real belongs to some countable Scott set, referred to via reals that uniformly enumerate it.
statement.facts: Equivalent to Weak König's Lemma over RCA0 (Lemma 8.18). Every countable model of RCA0 is an ω-submodel of a countable model of RCA0 + SS (Lemma 8.19).
